17.54.334.m: "When Vasiṣṭha performed sorcery against the Saudāsas, in this way indeed he performed sorcery against them.

17.54.334.s: keśī ha yatra khāṇḍikam abhicacāraivam̐ hainam abhicacāra
17.54.334.d: केशी ह यत्र खाण्डिकम् अभिचचारैवँ हैनम् अभिचचार
17.54.334.m: When Keśin performed sorcery against Khāṇḍika, in this way indeed he performed sorcery against him.

17.54.334.s: sārvasenir ha yatra bhrātṛvyān abhicacāraivam̐ hainān abhicacāra ||
17.54.334.d: सार्वसेनिर् ह यत्र भ्रातृव्यान् अभिचचारैवँ हैनान् अभिचचार ॥
17.54.334.m: When Sārvaseni performed sorcery against his rivals, in this way indeed he performed sorcery against them."

17.55.334.s: cāturmāsyaiḥ somair yakṣyamāṇo bhavati sa dvayān saṃbhārān upakalpayata āgniṣṭomikām̐ś ca vaiśvadevasaṃbhārām̐ś ca
17.55.334.d: चातुर्मास्यैः सोमैर् यक्ष्यमाणो भवति स द्वयान् संभारान् उपकल्पयत आग्निष्टोमिकाँश् च वैश्वदेवसंभाराँश् च
17.55.334.m: One is going to sacrifice with the seasonal soma sacrifices. / He prepares two sets of materials: those for an agniṣṭoma and those for the Vaiśvadeva.

17.55.334.s: sa purastāt phālgunyai vā caitryai vā paurṇamāsyā āmāvāsyena haviṣeṣṭvā dīkṣate
17.55.334.d: स पुरस्तात् फाल्गुन्यै वा चैत्र्यै वा पौर्णमास्या आमावास्येन हविषेष्ट्वा दीक्षते
17.55.334.m: Before the full moon of Phālguna or of Caitra, having sacrificed with the oblation of the new moon ritual, he undergoes consecration.

17.55.334.s: tasyāparimitā dīkṣās tisra upasadaḥ sa tathā rājānaṃ krīṇāti yathā manyate paurṇamāsyai me yajñiye 'han sutyā saṃpatsyata iti
17.55.334.d: तस्यापरिमिता दीक्षास् तिस्र उपसदः स तथा राजानं क्रीणाति यथा मन्यते पौर्णमास्यै मे यज्ञिये ऽहन् सुत्या संपत्स्यत इति
17.55.334.m: For him there are an unlimited number of consecration days and three upasads. / He buys the King [Soma] in such a way that he thinks, "My pressing will take place on the sacrificial day of the full moon."

17.55.334.s: tasya tathā saṃpadyate prasiddhena karmaṇopavasathād eti |
17.55.334.d: तस्य तथा संपद्यते प्रसिद्धेन कर्मणोपवसथाद् एति ।
17.55.334.m: It turns out thus for him. / He proceeds up to the fast-day by the standard procedure.

17.55.334.s: athāsyaitad ahar viśvebhyo devebhyo vatsā apākṛtā bhavanti
17.55.334.d: अथास्यैतद् अहर् विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो वत्सा अपाकृता भवन्ति
17.55.334.m: Then on this day calves are separated [from the cows] for the All-Gods.

17.55.334.s: vaiśvadevaṃ payo dohayati sāṃnāyyasya vāvṛtā tūṣṇīṃ vā | atha vasatīvarīḥ parihṛtya payām̐si viśiṣyopavasanti |
17.55.334.d: वैश्वदेवं पयो दोहयति सांनाय्यस्य वावृता तूष्णीं वा । अथ वसतीवरीः परिहृत्य पयाँसि विशिष्योपवसन्ति ।
17.55.334.m: He causes milk for the All-Gods to be milked, either according to the rite of the curd-and-milk oblation or silently. / Then having carried round the vasatīvarī waters and set aside the portions of milk, they fast.
Then in the morning, there is three-layered sacrificial grass.

17.55.334.s: tad ekavad eva stṛṇāti | athāgneyaṃ paśum upākaroti tasya vaiśvadeva upālambhyo bhavati
17.55.334.d: तद् एकवद् एव स्तृणाति । अथाग्नेयं पशुम् उपाकरोति तस्य वैश्वदेव उपालम्भ्यो भवति
17.55.334.m: He spreads it just as a single [layer]. / Then he brings forward the animal for Agni; / an [animal] for the All-Gods is to be immolated as its additional offering.
Following the morning-pressing offerings of that [animal], the oblations for the All-Gods follow.

17.55.334.s: praiṣavantaḥ savanīyās | anubrūhi yaja | itītareṣām̐ haviṣām
17.55.334.d: प्रैषवन्तः सवनीयास् । अनुब्रूहि यज । इतीतरेषाँ हविषाम्
17.55.334.m: The pressing-offerings have calls; / "Recite," "Sacrifice" are [the commands] for the other oblations.

17.55.335.s: ṛjudhā trivṛd agniṣṭomaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate purastād dhānāsomānāṃ vājinena carati
17.55.335.d: ऋजुधा त्रिवृद् अग्निष्टोमः संतिष्ठते पुरस्ताद् धानासोमानां वाजिनेन चरति
17.55.335.m: The threefold agniṣṭoma concludes straightway. Before the soma-grains, he proceeds with the whey.
The rite is the same up to the final bath. The final bath is well-known.
Having performed the concluding sacrifice, he dedicates a barren cow to Mitra and Varuṇa.

17.55.335.s: tasyai dyāvāpṛthivyopālambhyā bhavati tayoḥ prasiddhaṃ vapābhyāṃ caritvā paśupuroḍāśau nirvapati
17.55.335.d: तस्यै द्यावापृथिव्योपालम्भ्या भवति तयोः प्रसिद्धं वपाभ्यां चरित्वा पशुपुरोडाशौ निर्वपति
17.55.335.m: For it, a [female victim] for Heaven and Earth is to be additionally seized. Having proceeded with their two omenta in the well-known manner, he pours out the two animal-cakes.
It is completed in the same way as an animal sacrifice with two victims.

17.55.335.s: atha paurṇamāsavaimṛdhābhyām iṣṭvety uktam etad athātaś caturṣu māseṣu ||
17.55.335.d: अथ पौर्णमासवैमृधाभ्याम् इष्ट्वेत्य् उक्तम् एतद् अथातश् चतुर्षु मासेषु ॥
17.55.335.m: Now, having sacrificed with the full moon sacrifice and the Vaimṛdha sacrifice—this has already been stated. Now after four months:

17.56.335.m: He is about to sacrifice with the two soma-offerings of the Varuṇapraghāsa. He undergoes initiation.

17.56.335.s: tasyāparimitā dīkṣā dvādaśopasadaḥ sa tathā rājānaṃ krīṇāti yathā manyate paurṇamāsyai me yajñiye 'han dvitīyam ahaḥ saṃpatsyata iti
17.56.335.d: तस्यापरिमिता दीक्षा द्वादशोपसदः स तथा राजानं क्रीणाति यथा मन्यते पौर्णमास्यै मे यज्ञिये ऽहन् द्वितीयम् अहः संपत्स्यत इति
17.56.335.m: His initiation is of indefinite duration, [and there are] twelve upasad days. He buys King [Soma] in such a way that he thinks: 'My second day will coincide with the sacrificial day of the full moon.'

17.56.335.s: tasya tathā saṃpadyate prasiddhena karmaṇopavasathād eti |
17.56.335.d: तस्य तथा संपद्यते प्रसिद्धेन कर्मणोपवसथाद् एति ।
17.56.335.m: It comes to pass for him accordingly. He proceeds according to the well-known rite up to the fast-day.

17.56.335.s: athāsyaitad ahar marudbhyo vatsā apākṛtā bhavanti mārutaṃ payo dohayati sāṃnāyyasya vāvṛtā tūṣṇīṃ vā |
17.56.335.d: अथास्यैतद् अहर् मरुद्भ्यो वत्सा अपाकृता भवन्ति मारुतं पयो दोहयति सांनाय्यस्य वावृता तूष्णीं वा ।
17.56.335.m: Then on this day the calves are separated for the Maruts. He has milk milked for the Maruts, either according to the procedure of the curd-and-milk oblation or silently.
Then, having carried the vasatīvarī waters around, having left over milk, they fast.
Then in the morning he dedicates the victim to Agni.

17.56.335.s: tasya māruta upālambhyo bhavati tasya prātaḥsavanīyān anuvartante sapta varuṇapraghāsahavīm̐ṣi
17.56.335.d: तस्य मारुत उपालम्भ्यो भवति तस्य प्रातःसवनीयान् अनुवर्तन्ते सप्त वरुणप्रघासहवीँषि
17.56.335.m: To it, a [victim] for the Maruts is to be additionally seized. The seven Varuṇapraghāsa oblations follow its morning pressing-oblations.

17.56.335.s: sa yatra prātaḥsavane dhiṣṇiyān viharati tad ajasraṃ mārjālīyaṃ karoti
17.56.335.d: स यत्र प्रातःसवने धिष्णियान् विहरति तद् अजस्रं मार्जालीयं करोति
17.56.335.m: When he distributes the side-hearths at the morning pressing, he makes the mārjālīya [hearth] continuous [with fire].

17.56.335.s: samāsanneṣu haviḥṣu gārhapatye karambhapātrāṇy abhiparyagnikṛtvā tair mārjālīye pracarati
17.56.335.d: समासन्नेषु हविःषु गार्हपत्ये करम्भपात्राण्य् अभिपर्यग्निकृत्वा तैर् मार्जालीये प्रचरति
17.56.335.m: When the oblations have been set down, having carried fire around the pots of groats at the gārhapatya, he proceeds with them on the mārjālīya.

17.56.335.s: praiṣavantaḥ savanīyās | anubrūhi yaja | itītareṣām̐ haviṣām
17.56.335.d: प्रैषवन्तः सवनीयास् । अनुब्रूहि यज । इतीतरेषाँ हविषाम्
17.56.335.m: The pressing-oblations have calls of instruction; 'Recite', 'Offer' [are said] for the other oblations.

17.56.335.s: ṛjudhā pañcadaśa ukthyaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate | ahīnasaṃtatiṃ karoti |
17.56.335.d: ऋजुधा पञ्चदश उक्थ्यः संतिष्ठते । अहीनसंततिं करोति ।
17.56.335.m: The fifteenfold ukthya concludes straightway. He performs the continuity of the ahīna.

17.56.336.s: athāsyaitad ahar varuṇāya vatsā apākṛtā bhavanti vāruṇaṃ payo dohayati sāṃnāyyasya vāvṛtā tūṣṇīṃ vā |
17.56.336.d: अथास्यैतद् अहर् वरुणाय वत्सा अपाकृता भवन्ति वारुणं पयो दोहयति सांनाय्यस्य वावृता तूष्णीं वा ।
17.56.336.m: Then on this day the calves are separated for Varuṇa. He has milk milked for Varuṇa, either according to the procedure of the curd-and-milk oblation or silently.
Then, having carried the vasatīvarī waters around, having left over milk, they fast.
Then in the morning he dedicates the victim to Agni.

17.56.336.s: tasya vāruṇa upālambhyo bhavati tasya prātaḥsavanīyān anuvartete vāruṇī ca kāyaś ca
17.56.336.d: तस्य वारुण उपालम्भ्यो भवति तस्य प्रातःसवनीयान् अनुवर्तेते वारुणी च कायश् च
17.56.336.m: To it, a [victim] for Varuṇa is to be additionally seized. The oblation to Varuṇa and that to Ka follow its morning pressing-oblations.
The pressing-oblations have calls of instruction;

17.56.336.s: anubrūhi yaja | itītarayor haviṣos | ṛjudhā saptadaśa ukthyaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate
17.56.336.d: अनुब्रूहि यज । इतीतरयोर् हविषोस् । ऋजुधा सप्तदश उक्थ्यः संतिष्ठते
17.56.336.m: 'Recite', 'Offer' [are said] for the other two oblations. The seventeenfold ukthya concludes straightway.

17.56.336.s: purastād dhānāsomānāṃ vājinābhyāṃ carati samānaṃ karmāvabhṛtāt |
17.56.336.d: पुरस्ताद् धानासोमानां वाजिनाभ्यां चरति समानं कर्मावभृतात् ।
17.56.336.m: Before the soma-grains, he proceeds with the two wheys. The rite is the same up to the final bath.

17.56.336.s: athaitasminn avabhṛtha upādadate vāruṇyai niṣkāsaṃ tuṣān iti
17.56.336.d: अथैतस्मिन्न् अवभृथ उपाददते वारुण्यै निष्कासं तुषान् इति
17.56.336.m: Then at this final bath they take up the scraping for Varuṇa [and] the husks.

17.56.336.s: vāruṇasya vāruṇyāmikṣādhyavadānīyā bhavati | ṛjīṣeṇa saha tuṣān saṃprakiranti
17.56.336.d: वारुणस्य वारुण्यामिक्षाध्यवदानीया भवति । ऋजीषेण सह तुषान् संप्रकिरन्ति
17.56.336.m: The curds of the offering to Varuṇa are to be additionally portioned into that for Varuṇa. They scatter the husks together with the soma-dregs.

17.56.336.d: प्रसिद्धो ऽवभृथस् । उदयनीययेष्ट्येष्ट्वा मैत्रावरुणीं वशाम् उपाकरोति
17.56.336.m: The final bath is well-known. Having performed the concluding sacrifice, he dedicates a barren cow to Mitra and Varuṇa.

17.56.336.s: tasyai kāyopālambhyā bhavati tayoḥ prasiddhaṃ vapābhyāṃ caritvā paśupuroḍāśau nirvapati
17.56.336.d: तस्यै कायोपालम्भ्या भवति तयोः प्रसिद्धं वपाभ्यां चरित्वा पशुपुरोडाशौ निर्वपति
17.56.336.m: For it, a [female victim] for Ka is to be additionally seized. Having proceeded with their two omenta in the well-known manner, he pours out the two animal-cakes.
It is completed in the same way as an animal sacrifice with two victims.
Now, having sacrificed with the full moon sacrifice and the Vaimṛdha sacrifice—this has already been stated.

17.57.336.s: sākamedhaiḥ somair yakṣyamāṇo bhavati dīkṣate tasyāparimitā dīkṣā dvādaśopasadaḥ
17.57.336.d: साकमेधैः सोमैर् यक्ष्यमाणो भवति दीक्षते तस्यापरिमिता दीक्षा द्वादशोपसदः
17.57.336.m: He is about to sacrifice with the Sākamedha soma-offerings. He undergoes initiation. His initiation is of indefinite duration, [and there are] twelve upasad days.

17.57.336.s: sa tathā rājānaṃ krīṇāti yathā manyate paurṇamāsyai me yajñiye 'han tṛtīyam ahaḥ saṃpatsyata iti
17.57.336.d: स तथा राजानं क्रीणाति यथा मन्यते पौर्णमास्यै मे यज्ञिये ऽहन् तृतीयम् अहः संपत्स्यत इति
17.57.336.m: He buys King [Soma] in such a way that he thinks: 'My third day will coincide with the sacrificial day of the full moon.'
It comes to pass for him accordingly.

17.57.336.s: prasiddhena karmaṇopavasathād eti | atha vasatīvarīḥ parihṛtya payām̐si viśiṣyopavasanti |
17.57.336.d: प्रसिद्धेन कर्मणोपवसथाद् एति । अथ वसतीवरीः परिहृत्य पयाँसि विशिष्योपवसन्ति ।
17.57.336.m: He proceeds according to the well-known rite up to the fast-day. Then, having carried the vasatīvarī waters around, having left over milk, they fast.
Then in the morning he dedicates the victim to Agni.

17.57.337.s: tasyānīkavata upālambhyo bhavati tasya prātaḥsavanīyān anuvartata ānīkavataḥ
17.57.337.d: तस्यानीकवत उपालम्भ्यो भवति तस्य प्रातःसवनीयान् अनुवर्तत आनीकवतः
17.57.337.m: To it, a [victim] for [Agni] Anīkavat is to be additionally seized. The oblation to [Agni] Anīkavat follows its morning pressing-oblations.

17.57.337.s: praiṣavantaḥ savanīyās | anubrūhi yaja | ity ānīkavatasya
17.57.337.d: प्रैषवन्तः सवनीयास् । अनुब्रूहि यज । इत्य् आनीकवतस्य
17.57.337.m: The pressing-oblations have calls of instruction; 'Recite', 'Offer' [are said] for the oblation to Anīkavat.
The oblation to the Sāṃtapanas follows the midday pressing-oblations. The pressing-oblations have calls of instruction;

17.57.337.s: anubrūhi yaja | iti sāṃtapanasya | ṛjudhaikavim̐śa ukthyaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate |
17.57.337.d: अनुब्रूहि यज । इति सांतपनस्य । ऋजुधैकविँश उक्थ्यः संतिष्ठते ।
17.57.337.m: 'Recite', 'Offer' [are said] for the oblation to the Sāṃtapanas. The twenty-onefold ukthya concludes straightway.

17.57.337.s: ahīnasaṃsatiṃ karoti | atha vasatīvarīḥ parihṛtya payām̐si viśiṣyopavasanti |
17.57.337.d: अहीनसंसतिं करोति । अथ वसतीवरीः परिहृत्य पयाँसि विशिष्योपवसन्ति ।
17.57.337.m: He performs the continuity of the ahīna. Then, having carried the vasatīvarī waters around, having left over milk, they fast.

17.57.337.s: atha sāyaṃ gṛhamedhīyena carati | athāpararātre pūrṇadarvyenā carati |
17.57.337.d: अथ सायं गृहमेधीयेन चरति । अथापररात्रे पूर्णदर्व्येना चरति ।
17.57.337.m: Then in the evening he proceeds with the Gṛhamedhīya oblation. Then in the latter part of the night he proceeds with the full ladle [oblation].

17.57.337.s: atha prātar āgneyaṃ paśum upākaroti tasya kraiḍina upālambhyo bhavati
17.57.337.d: अथ प्रातर् आग्नेयं पशुम् उपाकरोति तस्य क्रैडिन उपालम्भ्यो भवति
17.57.337.m: Then in the morning he dedicates the victim to Agni. To it, a [victim] for the Kraiḍin [Maruts] is to be additionally seized.
The oblation to the Kraiḍins follows its morning pressing-oblations.

17.57.337.s: praiṣavantaḥ savanīyās | anubrūhi yaja | iti kraiḍinasya | ṛjudhā triṇava ukthyaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate |
17.57.337.d: प्रैषवन्तः सवनीयास् । अनुब्रूहि यज । इति क्रैडिनस्य । ऋजुधा त्रिणव उक्थ्यः संतिष्ठते ।
17.57.337.m: The pressing-oblations have calls of instruction; 'Recite', 'Offer' [are said] for the oblation to the Kraiḍins. The twenty-sevenfold ukthya concludes straightway.

17.57.337.s: ahīnasaṃtatiṃ karoti | atha vasatīvarīḥ parihṛtya payām̐si viśiṣyopavasanti |
17.57.337.d: अहीनसंततिं करोति । अथ वसतीवरीः परिहृत्य पयाँसि विशिष्योपवसन्ति ।
17.57.337.m: He performs the continuity of the ahīna. Then, having carried the vasatīvarī waters around, having left over milk, they fast.
Then in the morning he dedicates the victim to Agni.

17.57.337.s: tasya prājāpatyas tūpara upālambhyo bhavati tasya prātaḥsavanīyān anuvartante mahāhavīm̐ṣi
17.57.337.d: तस्य प्राजापत्यस् तूपर उपालम्भ्यो भवति तस्य प्रातःसवनीयान् अनुवर्तन्ते महाहवीँषि
17.57.337.m: To it, a hornless [victim] for Prajāpati is to be additionally seized. The great oblations follow its morning pressing-oblations.
The pressing-oblations have calls of instruction;

17.57.337.s: anubrūhi yaja | itītareṣām̐ haviṣām | tṛtīyasavanīyān anuvartante mahāpitṛyajñahavīm̐ṣi
17.57.337.d: अनुब्रूहि यज । इतीतरेषाँ हविषाम् । तृतीयसवनीयान् अनुवर्तन्ते महापितृयज्ञहवीँषि
17.57.337.m: 'Recite', 'Offer' [are said] for the other oblations. The oblations of the great ancestral sacrifice follow the third pressing-oblations.

17.57.337.s: sa yatra tṛtīyasavane dhiṣṇiyān viharati tad ajasraṃ mārjālīyaṃ karoti
17.57.337.d: स यत्र तृतीयसवने धिष्णियान् विहरति तद् अजस्रं मार्जालीयं करोति
17.57.337.m: When he distributes the side-hearths at the third pressing, he makes the mārjālīya [hearth] continuous [with fire].

17.57.337.s: samāsanneṣu haviḥṣu gārhapatye mahāpitṛyajñahavīm̐ṣi śrapayitvā tair mārjālīye pracarati
17.57.337.d: समासन्नेषु हविःषु गार्हपत्ये महापितृयज्ञहवीँषि श्रपयित्वा तैर् मार्जालीये प्रचरति
17.57.337.m: When the oblations have been set down, having cooked the oblations of the great ancestral sacrifice on the gārhapatya, he proceeds with them on the mārjālīya.

17.57.337.s: praiṣavantaḥ savanīyās | anubrūhi yaja | itītareṣām̐ haviṣām
17.57.337.d: प्रैषवन्तः सवनीयास् । अनुब्रूहि यज । इतीतरेषाँ हविषाम्
17.57.337.m: The pressing-oblations have calls of instruction; 'Recite', 'Offer' [are said] for the other oblations.

17.57.337.s: ṛjudhā trayastrim̐śa ukthyaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate purastād dhānāsomānāṃ traiyambhakaiś carati
17.57.337.d: ऋजुधा त्रयस्त्रिँश उक्थ्यः संतिष्ठते पुरस्ताद् धानासोमानां त्रैयम्भकैश् चरति
17.57.337.m: The thirty-threefold ukthya concludes straightway. Before the soma-grains, he proceeds with the Traiyambaka oblations.

17.57.337.s: samānaṃ karmāvabhṛthāt prasiddho 'vabhṛthas | udayanīyayeṣṭyeṣṭvā maitrāvaruṇīṃ vaśām upākaroti
17.57.337.d: समानं कर्मावभृथात् प्रसिद्धो ऽवभृथस् । उदयनीययेष्ट्येष्ट्वा मैत्रावरुणीं वशाम् उपाकरोति
17.57.337.m: The rite is the same up to the final bath. The final bath is well-known. Having performed the concluding sacrifice, he dedicates a barren cow to Mitra and Varuṇa.

17.57.338.m: For it, a [female victim] for Viśvakarman is to be additionally seized.

17.57.338.s: tayoḥ prasiddhaṃ vapābhyāṃ caritvā paśupuroḍāśau nirvapati
17.57.338.d: तयोः प्रसिद्धं वपाभ्यां चरित्वा पशुपुरोडाशौ निर्वपति
17.57.338.m: Having proceeded with their two omenta in the well-known manner, he pours out the two animal-cakes.
The oblation to Āditya follows them. The two animal-cakes have calls of instruction.

17.57.338.s: anubrūhi yaja | ity ādityasya saṃtiṣṭhate yathā dvipaśuḥ paśubandhas tathā |
17.57.338.d: अनुब्रूहि यज । इत्य् आदित्यस्य संतिष्ठते यथा द्विपशुः पशुबन्धस् तथा ।
17.57.338.m:
"Recite," "Sacrifice" are [the formulas] for the [offering] to Āditya.
It concludes in the manner of an animal sacrifice with two animals.

17.57.338.s: atha paurṇamāsavaimṛdhābhyām iṣṭvety uktam etad athātaś caturṣu māseṣu ||
17.57.338.d: अथ पौर्णमासवैमृधाभ्याम् इष्ट्वेत्य् उक्तम् एतद् अथातश् चतुर्षु मासेषु ॥
17.57.338.m:
Then, having performed the full moon sacrifice and the Vaimṛdha offering—this has [already] been stated.
Now then, after four months,

17.58.338.m:
he is going to sacrifice with the Śunāsīrīya Soma sacrifice.
He undergoes consecration.

17.58.338.s: tasyāparimitā dīkṣāstisra upasadaḥ sa tathā rājānaṃ krīṇāti yathā manyate paurṇamāsye me yajñiye 'han sutyā saṃpatsyata iti
17.58.338.d: तस्यापरिमिता दीक्षास्तिस्र उपसदः स तथा राजानं क्रीणाति यथा मन्यते पौर्णमास्ये मे यज्ञिये ऽहन् सुत्या संपत्स्यत इति
17.58.338.m:
His consecrations are unlimited [in number]; there are three Upasads.
He purchases the King [Soma] in such a way that he thinks: "My pressing day will fall on the sacrificial day of the full moon."

For him it falls accordingly.
He proceeds with the established procedure up to the fast-day.

17.58.338.s: atha vasatīvarīḥ parihṛtya payām̐si viśiṣyopavasanti | athāsyaitām̐ rātriṃ vāyave vatsā apākṛtā bhavanti
17.58.338.d: अथ वसतीवरीः परिहृत्य पयाँसि विशिष्योपवसन्ति । अथास्यैताँ रात्रिं वायवे वत्सा अपाकृता भवन्ति
17.58.338.m:
Then, having carried around the vasatīvarī waters and set aside the milks, they observe the fast.
Then, on this night, the calves are separated for Vāyu.

17.58.338.s: prātar vāyavyaṃ payo dohayati sāṃnāyyasya vāvṛtā tūṣṇīṃ vā |
17.58.338.d: प्रातर् वायव्यं पयो दोहयति सांनाय्यस्य वावृता तूष्णीं वा ।
17.58.338.m: In the morning he has the milk for Vāyu milked, either according to the rite of the curd-and-milk oblation or silently.
Then he dedicates the animal to Agni.

17.58.338.s: tasyaindra ṛṣabha upālambhyo bhavati tasya prātaḥsavanīyān anuvartante śunāsīrīyahavīm̐ṣi
17.58.338.d: तस्यैन्द्र ऋषभ उपालम्भ्यो भवति तस्य प्रातःसवनीयान् अनुवर्तन्ते शुनासीरीयहवीँषि
17.58.338.m:
A bull dedicated to Indra is to be seized as an additional victim along with it.
The Śunāsīrīya oblations follow after its morning press-cakes.
The press-cakes are accompanied by calls [to the hotṛ priest].

17.58.338.s: anubrūhi yaja | itītareṣāṃ haviṣām ṛjudhā jyotiragniṣṭomaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate
17.58.338.d: अनुब्रूहि यज । इतीतरेषां हविषाम् ऋजुधा ज्योतिरग्निष्टोमः संतिष्ठते
17.58.338.m:
"Recite," "Sacrifice" [are the calls] for the other oblations.
The Jyotiragniṣṭoma concludes straightway.

17.58.338.s: samānaṃ karmāvabhṛthāt prasiddho 'vabhṛthas | udayanīyayeṣṭyeṣṭvā maitrāvaruṇīṃ vaśām upākaroti
17.58.338.d: समानं कर्मावभृथात् प्रसिद्धो ऽवभृथस् । उदयनीययेष्ट्येष्ट्वा मैत्रावरुणीं वशाम् उपाकरोति
17.58.338.m:
The procedure up to the final bath is identical.
The final bath is well established.
Having sacrificed with the concluding offering, he dedicates a barren cow to Mitra and Varuṇa.
A cow dedicated to Sūrya is to be seized as an additional victim along with it.

17.58.338.s: tayoḥ prasiddhaṃ vapābhyāṃ caritvā paśupuroḍāśau nirvapti
17.58.338.d: तयोः प्रसिद्धं वपाभ्यां चरित्वा पशुपुरोडाशौ निर्वप्ति
17.58.338.m: Having performed the offering of their omenta according to the established manner, he dispenses the two animal-cake portions.

17.58.339.s: saṃtiṣṭhate yathā dvipaśuḥ paśubandhas tathā | atha paurṇamāsavaimṛdhābhyām iṣṭvety uktam etat ||
17.58.339.d: संतिष्ठते यथा द्विपशुः पशुबन्धस् तथा । अथ पौर्णमासवैमृधाभ्याम् इष्ट्वेत्य् उक्तम् एतत् ॥
17.58.339.m:
It concludes in the manner of an animal sacrifice with two animals.
Then, having performed the full moon sacrifice and the Vaimṛdha offering—this has [already] been stated.

17.59.339.s: athāto jyotirayanam ity ācakṣate vaiśvadevena somena yakṣyamāṇo bhavati | iti samānī pratipat |
17.59.339.d: अथातो ज्योतिरयनम् इत्य् आचक्षते वैश्वदेवेन सोमेन यक्ष्यमाणो भवति । इति समानी प्रतिपत् ।
17.59.339.m:
Now then, they call [this] the Jyotirayana.
"He is going to sacrifice with the Vaiśvadeva Soma sacrifice"—the introductory procedure is identical.

Just this much is different:
there [in the basic paradigm] the agniṣṭoma is a ninefold chant;

17.59.339.s: jyotir iha | athātaś caturṣu māseṣu varuṇapraghāsena somena yakṣyamāṇo bhavati
17.59.339.d: ज्योतिर् इह । अथातश् चतुर्षु मासेषु वरुणप्रघासेन सोमेन यक्ष्यमाणो भवति
17.59.339.m:
here it is the Jyotis.
Now then, after four months, he is going to sacrifice with the Varuṇapraghāsa Soma sacrifice.

He undergoes consecration.
His consecrations are unlimited [in number]; there are six Upasads.

17.59.339.s: sa tathā rājānaṃ krīṇāti yathā manyate paurṇamāsyai me yajñiye 'han sutyā saṃpatsyata iti
17.59.339.d: स तथा राजानं क्रीणाति यथा मन्यते पौर्णमास्यै मे यज्ञिये ऽहन् सुत्या संपत्स्यत इति
17.59.339.m: He purchases the King [Soma] in such a way that he thinks: "My pressing day will fall on the sacrificial day of the full moon."

17.59.339.s: prasiddhena karmaṇopavasathād eti | athāsyaitad ahar dvayā vatsā apākṛtā bhavanti marudbhyo varuṇāyeti
17.59.339.d: प्रसिद्धेन कर्मणोपवसथाद् एति । अथास्यैतद् अहर् द्वया वत्सा अपाकृता भवन्ति मरुद्भ्यो वरुणायेति
17.59.339.m:
He proceeds with the established procedure up to the fast-day.
Then, on this day, two kinds of calves are separated: for the Maruts and for Varuṇa.

17.59.339.s: dvayaṃ payo dohayati sāṃnāyyasya vāvṛtā tūṣṇīṃ vā |
17.59.339.d: द्वयं पयो दोहयति सांनाय्यस्य वावृता तूष्णीं वा ।
17.59.339.m: He has two kinds of milk milked, either according to the rite of the curd-and-milk oblation or silently.
Then, having carried around the vasatīvarī waters and set aside the milks, they observe the fast.
Then in the morning he dedicates the animal to Agni.

17.59.339.s: tasya māruto vāruṇa ity upālambhyau bhavatas tasya prātaḥsavanīyān anuvartante sapta varuṇapraghāsahavīm̐ṣi
17.59.339.d: तस्य मारुतो वारुण इत्य् उपालम्भ्यौ भवतस् तस्य प्रातःसवनीयान् अनुवर्तन्ते सप्त वरुणप्रघासहवीँषि
17.59.339.m:
Two [animals], one for the Maruts and one for Varuṇa, are to be seized as additional victims along with it.
The seven Varuṇapraghāsa oblations follow after its morning press-cakes.

17.59.339.s: sa yatra prātaḥsavane dhiṣṇiyān viharati tad ajasraṃ mārjālīyaṃ karoti
17.59.339.d: स यत्र प्रातःसवने धिष्णियान् विहरति तद् अजस्रं मार्जालीयं करोति
17.59.339.m: Where he distributes the side-hearths at the morning pressing, there he makes the mārjālīya hearth unquenched.

17.59.339.s: samāsanneṣu haviḥṣu gārhapatye karambhapātrāṇy abhiparyagnikṛtvā tair mārjālīye pracarati
17.59.339.d: समासन्नेषु हविःषु गार्हपत्ये करम्भपात्राण्य् अभिपर्यग्निकृत्वा तैर् मार्जालीये प्रचरति
17.59.339.m: When the oblations have been set down, having carried fire around the dishes of groats at the gārhapatya fire, he performs the ritual with them at the mārjālīya hearth.

17.59.339.s: praiṣavantaḥ savanīyās | anubrūhi yaja | itītareṣām̐ haviṣām |
17.59.339.d: प्रैषवन्तः सवनीयास् । अनुब्रूहि यज । इतीतरेषाँ हविषाम् ।
17.59.339.m:
The press-cakes are accompanied by calls;
"Recite," "Sacrifice" [are the calls] for the other oblations.

17.59.339.s: mādhyaṃdinīyān anuvartete vāruṇī ca kāyaś ca praiṣavantaḥ savanīyās |
17.59.339.d: माध्यंदिनीयान् अनुवर्तेते वारुणी च कायश् च प्रैषवन्तः सवनीयास् ।
17.59.339.m:
The oblation to Varuṇa and the oblation to Ka follow after the midday press-cakes.
The press-cakes are accompanied by calls;

17.59.339.s: anubrūhi yaja | itītarayor haviṣos | ṛjudhā jyotir ukthyaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate
17.59.339.d: अनुब्रूहि यज । इतीतरयोर् हविषोस् । ऋजुधा ज्योतिर् उक्थ्यः संतिष्ठते
17.59.339.m:
"Recite," "Sacrifice" [are the calls] for the other two oblations.
The Jyotirukthya concludes straightway.

17.59.339.s: samānam uttaraṃ karma yathā dvirātre tathā | athātaś caturṣu māseṣu ||
17.59.339.d: समानम् उत्तरं कर्म यथा द्विरात्रे तथा । अथातश् चतुर्षु मासेषु ॥
17.59.339.m:
The subsequent procedure is identical, as in a two-day rite.
Now then, after four months,

17.60.340.s: sākamedhena somena yakṣyamāṇo bhavati dīkṣate tasyāparimitā dīkṣāḥ ṣaḍ upasadaḥ
17.60.340.d: साकमेधेन सोमेन यक्ष्यमाणो भवति दीक्षते तस्यापरिमिता दीक्षाः षड् उपसदः
17.60.340.m:
he is going to sacrifice with the Sākamedha Soma sacrifice.
He undergoes consecration.
His consecrations are unlimited [in number]; there are six Upasads.

17.60.340.s: sa tathā rājānaṃ krīṇāti yathā manyate paurṇamāsyai me yajñiye 'han sutyā saṃpatsyata iti
17.60.340.d: स तथा राजानं क्रीणाति यथा मन्यते पौर्णमास्यै मे यज्ञिये ऽहन् सुत्या संपत्स्यत इति
17.60.340.m: He purchases the King [Soma] in such a way that he thinks: "My pressing day will fall on the sacrificial day of the full moon."

17.60.340.s: tasya tathā saṃpadyate prasiddhena karmaṇopavasathād eti | atha vasatīvarīḥ parihṛtya payām̐si viśiṣyopavasanti |
17.60.340.d: तस्य तथा संपद्यते प्रसिद्धेन कर्मणोपवसथाद् एति । अथ वसतीवरीः परिहृत्य पयाँसि विशिष्योपवसन्ति ।
17.60.340.m:
For him it falls accordingly.
He proceeds with the established procedure up to the fast-day.
Then, having carried around the vasatīvarī waters and set aside the milks, they observe the fast.
Then in the morning he dedicates the animal to Agni.

17.60.340.s: tasyānīkavataḥ kraiḍinaḥ prājāpatyas tūpara ity upālambhyā bhavanti
17.60.340.d: तस्यानीकवतः क्रैडिनः प्राजापत्यस् तूपर इत्य् उपालम्भ्या भवन्ति
17.60.340.m: Victims dedicated to [Agni] Anīkavat, the Kraiḍin [Maruts], and a hornless victim for Prajāpati are to be seized as additional victims along with it.
The oblation to [Agni] Anīkavat follows after its morning press-cakes.

17.60.340.s: praiṣavantaḥ savanīyās | anubrūhi yaja | ityānīkavatasya mādhyaṃdinīyān anuvartate sāṃtapanaḥ
17.60.340.d: प्रैषवन्तः सवनीयास् । अनुब्रूहि यज । इत्यानीकवतस्य माध्यंदिनीयान् अनुवर्तते सांतपनः

17.60.340.s: praiṣavantaḥ savanīyās | anubrūhi yaja | iti sāṃtapanasya
17.60.340.d: प्रैषवन्तः सवनीयास् । अनुब्रूहि यज । इति सांतपनस्य
17.60.340.m:
The press-cakes are accompanied by calls;
"Recite," "Sacrifice" are [the calls] for that to the Sāṃtapanas.
The great oblations beginning with the Gṛhamedhīya follow after the third pressing cakes.

17.60.340.s: sa yatra tṛtīyasavane dhiṣṇiyān viharati tad ajasraṃ mārjālīyaṃ karoti
17.60.340.d: स यत्र तृतीयसवने धिष्णियान् विहरति तद् अजस्रं मार्जालीयं करोति
17.60.340.m: Where he distributes the side-hearths at the third pressing, there he makes the mārjālīya hearth unquenched.

17.60.340.s: mahāhavirbhiś caritvā gārhapatye mahāpitṛyajñahavīm̐ṣi śrapayitvā tair mārjalīye pracarati
17.60.340.d: महाहविर्भिश् चरित्वा गार्हपत्ये महापितृयज्ञहवीँषि श्रपयित्वा तैर् मार्जलीये प्रचरति
17.60.340.m: Having performed the offering with the great oblations, and having cooked the Mahāpitṛyajña oblations on the gārhapatya fire, he performs the ritual with them at the mārjālīya hearth.

17.60.340.s: praiṣavantaḥ savanīyās | anubrūhi yaja | itītareṣām̐ haviṣām
17.60.340.d: प्रैषवन्तः सवनीयास् । अनुब्रूहि यज । इतीतरेषाँ हविषाम्
17.60.340.m:
The press-cakes are accompanied by calls;
"Recite," "Sacrifice" [are the calls] for the other oblations.

17.60.340.s: ṛjudhā jyotir ukthyaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate samānam uttaraṃ karma yathā trirātre tathā
17.60.340.d: ऋजुधा ज्योतिर् उक्थ्यः संतिष्ठते समानम् उत्तरं कर्म यथा त्रिरात्रे तथा
17.60.340.m:
The Jyotirukthya concludes straightway.
The subsequent procedure is identical, as in a three-day rite.

17.61.340.s: athāto mahāyajña ity ācakṣate jyotiratirātra ity eka āhus |
17.61.340.d: अथातो महायज्ञ इत्य् आचक्षते ज्योतिरतिरात्र इत्य् एक आहुस् ।
17.61.340.m:
Now then, they call [this] the Mahāyajña;
some call it the Jyotiratirātra.

17.61.340.s: dīkṣate tasyāparimitā dīkṣā dvādaśopasadaḥ sa tathā rājānaṃ krīṇāti yathā manyate paurṇamāsyai me yajñiye 'han sutyā saṃpatsyata iti
17.61.340.d: दीक्षते तस्यापरिमिता दीक्षा द्वादशोपसदः स तथा राजानं क्रीणाति यथा मन्यते पौर्णमास्यै मे यज्ञिये ऽहन् सुत्या संपत्स्यत इति
17.61.340.m:
He undergoes consecration.
His consecrations are unlimited [in number]; there are twelve Upasads.
He purchases the King [Soma] in such a way that he thinks: "My pressing day will fall on the sacrificial day of the full moon."

17.61.341.m:
For him it falls accordingly.
He proceeds with the established procedure up to the fast-day.

17.61.341.s: athāsyaitad ahas trayā vatsā apākṛtā bhavanti viśvebhyo devebhyo marudbhyo varuṇāyeti
17.61.341.d: अथास्यैतद् अहस् त्रया वत्सा अपाकृता भवन्ति विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो मरुद्भ्यो वरुणायेति
17.61.341.m: Then, on this day, three kinds of calves are separated: for the All-gods, for the Maruts, and for Varuṇa.

17.61.341.s: trayaṃ payo dohayati sāṃnāyyasya vāvṛtā tūṣṇīṃ vā |
17.61.341.d: त्रयं पयो दोहयति सांनाय्यस्य वावृता तूष्णीं वा ।
17.61.341.m: He has three kinds of milk milked, either according to the rite of the curd-and-milk oblation or silently.
Then, having carried around the vasatīvarī waters and set aside the milks, they observe the fast.

17.61.341.s: atha prātas trivṛd barhis tad ekavad eva stṛṇāti | athāgneyaṃ paśum upākaroti
17.61.341.d: अथ प्रातस् त्रिवृद् बर्हिस् तद् एकवद् एव स्तृणाति । अथाग्नेयं पशुम् उपाकरोति

17.61.341.s: tasya vaiśvadevo māruto vāruṇa ānīkavataḥ kraiḍinaḥ prājāpatyas tūpara aindra ṛṣabha ity upālambhyā bhavanti
17.61.341.d: तस्य वैश्वदेवो मारुतो वारुण आनीकवतः क्रैडिनः प्राजापत्यस् तूपर ऐन्द्र ऋषभ इत्य् उपालम्भ्या भवन्ति
17.61.341.m: Victims dedicated to the All-gods, to the Maruts, to Varuṇa, to [Agni] Anīkavat, to the Kraiḍin [Maruts], a hornless victim for Prajāpati, and a bull for Indra are to be seized as additional victims along with it.
The Vaiśvadeva oblations follow after its morning press-cakes.
The press-cakes are accompanied by calls.

17.61.341.s: anubrūhi yaja | itītareṣām̐ haviṣām | mādhyaṃdinīyān anuvartante sarvāṇi varuṇapraghāsahavīm̐ṣi ||
17.61.341.d: अनुब्रूहि यज । इतीतरेषाँ हविषाम् । माध्यंदिनीयान् अनुवर्तन्ते सर्वाणि वरुणप्रघासहवीँषि ॥
17.61.341.m:
"Recite," "Sacrifice" [are the calls] for the other oblations.
All the Varuṇapraghāsa oblations follow after the midday press-cakes.

17.62.341.s: sa yatra mādhyaṃdinīye savane dhiṣṇiyān viharati tad ajasraṃ mārjālīyaṃ karoti
17.62.341.d: स यत्र माध्यंदिनीये सवने धिष्णियान् विहरति तद् अजस्रं मार्जालीयं करोति
17.62.341.m: Where he distributes the side-hearths at the midday pressing, there he makes the mārjālīya hearth unquenched.

17.62.341.s: samāsanneṣu haviḥṣu gārhapatye karambhapātrāṇy abhiparyagnikṛtvā tair mārjālīye pracarati
17.62.341.d: समासन्नेषु हविःषु गार्हपत्ये करम्भपात्राण्य् अभिपर्यग्निकृत्वा तैर् मार्जालीये प्रचरति
17.62.341.m: When the oblations have been set down, having carried fire around the dishes of groats at the gārhapatya fire, he performs the ritual with them at the mārjālīya hearth.
The press-cakes are accompanied by calls.

17.62.341.s: anubrūhi yaja | itītareṣām̐ haviṣām | tṛtīyasavanīyān anuvartanta ānīkavataprabhṛtīni mahāhavīm̐ṣi
17.62.341.d: अनुब्रूहि यज । इतीतरेषाँ हविषाम् । तृतीयसवनीयान् अनुवर्तन्त आनीकवतप्रभृतीनि महाहवीँषि
17.62.341.m: The savanīya oblations have calls: 'Recite,' 'Offer' are those of the other oblations. The great oblations beginning with the Anīkavat [oblation] follow after the oblations of the third pressing.

17.62.341.s: sa yatra tṛtīyasavane dhiṣṇiyān viharati tad ajasraṃ mārjālīyaṃ karoti
17.62.341.d: स यत्र तृतीयसवने धिष्णियान् विहरति तद् अजस्रं मार्जालीयं करोति
17.62.341.m: When he distributes the dhiṣṇiya hearths at the third pressing, he then makes the mārjālīya [fire] continuous.

17.62.342.s: mahāhavirbhiś caritvā gārhapatye mahāpitṛyajñahavīm̐ṣi śrapayitvā tair mārjālīye pracarati
17.62.342.d: महाहविर्भिश् चरित्वा गार्हपत्ये महापितृयज्ञहवीँषि श्रपयित्वा तैर् मार्जालीये प्रचरति
17.62.342.m: Having performed the rituals with the great oblations and having cooked the oblations of the Mahāpitṛyajña on the gārhapatya, he performs the rites with them on the mārjālīya fire.

17.62.342.s: praiṣavantaḥ savanīyās | anubrūhi yaja | itītareṣām̐ haviṣām
17.62.342.d: प्रैषवन्तः सवनीयास् । अनुब्रूहि यज । इतीतरेषाँ हविषाम्
17.62.342.m: The savanīya oblations have calls: 'Recite,' 'Offer' are those of the other oblations.

17.62.342.s: ṛjudhā jyotiratirātraḥ saṃtiṣṭhate purastād dhānāsomānāṃ vājinaiś caritvā traiyambakaiś carati
17.62.342.d: ऋजुधा ज्योतिरतिरात्रः संतिष्ठते पुरस्ताद् धानासोमानां वाजिनैश् चरित्वा त्रैयम्बकैश् चरति
17.62.342.m: The straight Jyotiratirātra concludes. Before the roasted grain and soma cups, having performed the rite with the curds for the vājin, he performs the Traiyambaka rite.
The procedure is identical up to the avabhṛtha.

17.62.342.s: athaitasminn avabhṛtha upādadate vāruṇyai niṣkāsaṃ tuṣān iti
17.62.342.d: अथैतस्मिन्न् अवभृथ उपाददते वारुण्यै निष्कासं तुषान् इति
17.62.342.m: Now at this avabhṛtha, they take the scraping [of milk-curd] and the husks for Varuṇa.

17.62.342.s: vāruṇasya vāruṇyāmikṣādhyavadānīyā bhavati | ṛjīṣeṇa saha tuṣān saṃprakiranti
17.62.342.d: वारुणस्य वारुण्यामिक्षाध्यवदानीया भवति । ऋजीषेण सह तुषान् संप्रकिरन्ति
17.62.342.m: The āmikṣā curd for Varuṇa is to be cut up with the portion for Varuṇa; they scatter the husks together with the soma-dregs.

17.62.342.d: प्रसिद्धो ऽवभृथस् । उदयनीययेष्ट्येष्ट्वा मैत्रावरुणीं वशाम् उपाकरोति
17.62.342.m: The avabhṛtha is known. Having performed the udayanīyā iṣṭi, he dedicates the barren cow for Mitra-Varuṇa.

17.62.342.s: tasyai dyāvāpṛthivyā kāyā vaiśvakarmaṇī saurīty upālambhyā bhavanti
17.62.342.d: तस्यै द्यावापृथिव्या काया वैश्वकर्मणी सौरीत्य् उपालम्भ्या भवन्ति
17.62.342.m: Its [additional] victims to be seized are one for Heaven and Earth, one for Ka (Prajāpati), one for Viśvakarman, and one for Sūrya.

17.62.342.s: tāsāṃ prasiddhaṃ vapābhiś caritvā paśupuroḍāśān nirvapati
17.62.342.d: तासां प्रसिद्धं वपाभिश् चरित्वा पशुपुरोडाशान् निर्वपति
17.62.342.m: Having performed the rites with their omenta in the prescribed manner, he portions out the animal cake-oblations.
The Śunāsīrīya oblations beginning with the one for the Ādityas follow after them.

17.62.342.s: praiṣavantaḥ paśupuroḍāśās | anubrūhi yaja | itītareṣām̐ haviṣām |
17.62.342.d: प्रैषवन्तः पशुपुरोडाशास् । अनुब्रूहि यज । इतीतरेषाँ हविषाम् ।
17.62.342.m: The animal cakes have calls: 'Recite,' 'Offer' are those of the other oblations.
It concludes just as an animal sacrifice with five victims concludes.

17.62.342.s: atha paurṇamāsavaimṛdhābhyām iṣṭvā yajamānāyatana upaviśya treṇyā śalalyā lohitāyasasya ca kṣureṇa śīrṣanni ca vartayate pari ca vapate purastād evāgre 'tha dakṣiṇato 'tha paścād athottarato 'thopariṣṭāt
17.62.342.d: अथ पौर्णमासवैमृधाभ्याम् इष्ट्वा यजमानायतन उपविश्य त्रेण्या शलल्या लोहितायसस्य च क्षुरेण शीर्षन्नि च वर्तयते परि च वपते पुरस्ताद् एवाग्रे ऽथ दक्षिणतो ऽथ पश्चाद् अथोत्तरतो ऽथोपरिष्टात्
17.62.342.m: Then, having performed the full moon sacrifice and the Vaimṛdha sacrifice, sitting down in the sacrificer's seat, he rolls back [his hair] on the head and shaves around with a porcupine quill with three white spots and a razor of reddish bronze, first right in front, then on the south, then behind, then on the north, and then above.

17.62.342.s: saṃtiṣṭhante cāturmāsyāḥ somāḥ saṃtiṣṭhante cāturmāsyāḥ somāḥ ||
17.62.342.d: संतिष्ठन्ते चातुर्मास्याः सोमाः संतिष्ठन्ते चातुर्मास्याः सोमाः ॥
17.62.342.m: The seasonal soma sacrifices conclude; the seasonal soma sacrifices conclude.

18.1.343.s: bṛhaspatisavena yakṣyamāṇo bhavati sa upakalpayate 'śvacatustrim̐śā dakṣiṇāḥ kṛṣṇājinam̐ suvarṇarajatau ca rukmau parṇamayaṃ pātram ājyam abhiṣecanāya |
18.1.343.d: बृहस्पतिसवेन यक्ष्यमाणो भवति स उपकल्पयते ऽश्वचतुस्त्रिँशा दक्षिणाः कृष्णाजिनँ सुवर्णरजतौ च रुक्मौ पर्णमयं पात्रम् आज्यम् अभिषेचनाय ।
18.1.343.m: One who is about to sacrifice with the Bṛhaspatisava makes ready thirty-four [cows] with a horse as the sacrificial fees, a black antelope skin, two ornaments of gold and silver, a vessel of parṇa wood, and clarified butter for the unction.

18.1.343.s: atha vai brāhmaṇaṃ bhavati parisrajī hotā bhavaty aruṇo mirmiras triśukras | iti |
18.1.343.d: अथ वै ब्राह्मणं भवति परिस्रजी होता भवत्य् अरुणो मिर्मिरस् त्रिशुक्रस् । इति ।
18.1.343.m: Now indeed there is a brāhmaṇa passage: 'The hotṛ priest is garlanded, reddish, mirmira, and having three white marks.'

18.1.343.s: eṣa ha vai parisrajī yaḥ khalatiḥ parikeśyas |
18.1.343.d: एष ह वै परिस्रजी यः खलतिः परिकेश्यस् ।
18.1.343.m: He indeed is garlanded who is bald, having hair around the edge.

18.1.343.s: atha haiṣa mirmiro yaḥ śuklo viklidhas tilakavān piṅgākṣas |
18.1.343.d: अथ हैष मिर्मिरो यः शुक्लो विक्लिधस् तिलकवान् पिङ्गाक्षस् ।
18.1.343.m: Now he is mirmira who is white, leprous, spotted, and reddish-eyed.

18.1.343.s: atha haiṣa triśukro yas trivedas | dīkṣate
18.1.343.d: अथ हैष त्रिशुक्रो यस् त्रिवेदस् । दीक्षते
18.1.343.m: Now he has three white marks who knows the three Vedas. He undergoes consecration.

18.1.343.s: tasyaikarātrīṇasya somaṃ krīṇanti tisra upasadas tāyate trivṛdagniṣṭomo rathaṃtarasāmā pravargyavān gāyatrīṣv eka stomaḥ
18.1.343.d: तस्यैकरात्रीणस्य सोमं क्रीणन्ति तिस्र उपसदस् तायते त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमो रथंतरसामा प्रवर्ग्यवान् गायत्रीष्व् एक स्तोमः
18.1.343.m: For that one-day sacrifice, they purchase the soma. There are three upasads. A trivṛt agniṣṭoma is performed, having the rathaṃtara saman, having the pravargya, and having a single stoma on gāyatrī verses.

18.1.343.s: prajñātaṃ devasuvām̐ haviṣāṃ karaṇam | tasya bārhaspatyo 'tigrāhyas |
18.1.343.d: प्रज्ञातं देवसुवाँ हविषां करणम् । तस्य बार्हस्पत्यो ऽतिग्राह्यस् ।
18.1.343.m: The performance of the Devasū oblations is known. Its additional cup is the one for Bṛhaspati.

18.1.343.s: bārhaspatyaḥ paśur upālambhyaḥ samānam ābhiṣekasya kālāt | abhiṣekasya kāle yajamānāyatane kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvam uttaralomopastṛṇāti
18.1.343.d: बार्हस्पत्यः पशुर् उपालम्भ्यः समानम् आभिषेकस्य कालात् । अभिषेकस्य काले यजमानायतने कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमोपस्तृणाति
18.1.343.m: An animal victim for Bṛhaspati is to be seized. The procedure is identical up to the time of unction. At the time of unction, he spreads the black antelope skin on the sacrificer's seat, with its neck turned toward the east and its hair upward.

18.1.343.s: tad yajamānaṃ prāñcam upaveśya suvarṇarajatābhyām̐ rukmābhyāṃ paryupāsya parṇamaye pātra ājyam ānīyābhiṣiñcati bṛhaspatiḥ prathamaṃ jāyamānas | maho jyotiṣaḥ parame vyoman | saptāsyas tuvijāto raveṇa vi saptaraśmir adhamattamam̐si ||
18.1.343.d: तद् यजमानं प्राञ्चम् उपवेश्य सुवर्णरजताभ्याँ रुक्माभ्यां पर्युपास्य पर्णमये पात्र आज्यम् आनीयाभिषिञ्चति बृहस्पतिः प्रथमं जायमानस् । महो ज्योतिषः परमे व्योमन् । सप्तास्यस् तुविजातो रवेण वि सप्तरश्मिर् अधमत्तमँसि ॥
18.1.343.m: Having seated the sacrificer there facing east, having placed on him the two ornaments of gold and silver, and having brought clarified butter into the vessel of parṇa wood, he sprinkles him, [reciting:] 'Bṛhaspati, when first being born / from the great light in the highest firmament, / seven-mouthed, born mighty with a roar, / seven-rayed, blew away the darknesses.'

18.1.343.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyām̐ sarasvatyai vāco yantur yantreṇa bṛhaspatisavenābhiṣiñcāmi | iti
18.1.343.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर् बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्याँ सरस्वत्यै वाचो यन्तुर् यन्त्रेण बृहस्पतिसवेनाभिषिञ्चामि । इति
18.1.343.m: [And reciting:] 'On the impulse of the divine Savitar, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, with the restraint of Sarasvatī, the restrainer of speech, with the Bṛhaspatisava I sprinkle you.'

18.1.343.s: samunmṛṣṭe samutkrośantīti samānam ā mukhasya vimārjanāt ||
18.1.343.d: समुन्मृष्टे समुत्क्रोशन्तीति समानम् आ मुखस्य विमार्जनात् ॥
18.1.343.m: When he is wiped, they shout together; thus it is identical up to the wiping of the face.

18.2.344.s: tasya prātaḥsavane sanneṣu nārāśam̐seṣv ekādaśa dakṣiṇā nīyante |
18.2.344.d: तस्य प्रातःसवने सन्नेषु नाराशँसेष्व् एकादश दक्षिणा नीयन्ते ।
18.2.344.m: For this ritual, when the nārāśaṃsa cups are deposited at the morning pressing, eleven sacrificial fees are led forward.

18.2.344.s: ekādaśa mādhyaṃdine savane sanneṣu nārāśam̐seṣu | aśvadvādaśās tṛtīyasavane sanneṣu nārāśam̐seṣu
18.2.344.d: एकादश माध्यंदिने सवने सन्नेषु नाराशँसेषु । अश्वद्वादशास् तृतीयसवने सन्नेषु नाराशँसेषु
18.2.344.m: Eleven [are led forward] when the nārāśaṃsa cups are deposited at the midday pressing; twelve including the horse when the nārāśaṃsa cups are deposited at the third pressing.

18.2.344.s: mādhyaṃdina eva savane 'śvaṃ dadyād iti ha smāha maudgalyaḥ
18.2.344.d: माध्यंदिन एव सवने ऽश्वं दद्याद् इति ह स्माह मौद्गल्यः
18.2.344.m: He should give the horse only at the midday pressing—so used Maudgalya to say.
This indeed is a sacrifice that wipes clean.

18.2.344.s: sa yathā ha vā iyaṃ gaireyī nadī nimṛjaty evam̐ ha vā eṣa etena yajñakratuneṣṭvā pāpmānaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ nimṛjann eti
18.2.344.d: स यथा ह वा इयं गैरेयी नदी निमृजत्य् एवँ ह वा एष एतेन यज्ञक्रतुनेष्ट्वा पाप्मानं भ्रातृव्यं निमृजन्न् एति
18.2.344.m: Just as this mountain river sweeps away [all impurities], even so indeed does this [sacrificer], having sacrificed with this ritual, go on wiping clean his evil, his rival.

18.2.344.s: sa etasminn eva pūrvapakṣe catuṣṭomenāgniṣṭomena yajeta purā bhreṣāc chāntyai
18.2.344.d: स एतस्मिन्न् एव पूर्वपक्षे चतुष्टोमेनाग्निष्टोमेन यजेत पुरा भ्रेषाच् छान्त्यै
18.2.344.m: He should sacrifice in that very first fortnight with a catuṣṭoma agniṣṭoma, for appeasement before any misfortune happens.
A king who has sacrificed with the Rājasūya desires: 'May I be anointed with the Bṛhaspatisava.'

18.2.344.s: tad u vā āhus | na vai rājasūyābhiṣikto 'nyena yajñakratunābhiṣicyeta |
18.2.344.d: तद् उ वा आहुस् । न वै राजसूयाभिषिक्तो ऽन्येन यज्ञक्रतुनाभिषिच्येत ।
18.2.344.m: Regarding that, they indeed say: 'One anointed with the Rājasūya should not be anointed with any other ritual;

18.2.344.s: apratyavarohī ha bhavati | iti | ubhābhyāṃ brahmakṣatrābhyām abhiṣicyā ity abhiṣicyetaiveti
18.2.344.d: अप्रत्यवरोही ह भवति । इति । उभाभ्यां ब्रह्मक्षत्राभ्याम् अभिषिच्या इत्य् अभिषिच्येतैवेति
18.2.344.m: for he does not descend.' But [others say]: 'He should indeed be anointed, thinking: "May I be anointed with both spiritual authority and royal power!"'

18.2.344.s: dīkṣate tasya tisro dīkṣās tisra upasadaḥ
18.2.344.d: दीक्षते तस्य तिस्रो दीक्षास् तिस्र उपसदः
18.2.344.m: He undergoes consecration. For him there are three consecration days and three upasads.

18.2.344.s: samānam ābhiṣekasya kālāt | abhiṣekasya kāle mādhyaṃdinīyā evainaṃ camasā nimṛjanto yanti
18.2.344.d: समानम् आभिषेकस्य कालात् । अभिषेकस्य काले माध्यंदिनीया एवैनं चमसा निमृजन्तो यन्ति
18.2.344.m: The procedure is identical up to the time of unction. At the time of unction, the cups of the midday pressing indeed go wiping him clean.

18.2.345.s: rājā rājasūyena yakṣyamāṇa ādhyāyati triṣu varṇeṣv abhiṣikteṣv adhyabhiṣicyeya purohite sthapatau sūta iti
18.2.345.d: राजा राजसूयेन यक्ष्यमाण आध्यायति त्रिषु वर्णेष्व् अभिषिक्तेष्व् अध्यभिषिच्येय पुरोहिते स्थपतौ सूत इति
18.2.345.m: A king who is about to sacrifice with the Rājasūya ponders: 'May I be anointed above the three classes who have been anointed: over the domestic priest, over the governor, and over the charioteer.'

18.2.345.s: tasya tisro dīkṣās tisra upasadaḥ samānam ābhiṣekasya kālāt |
18.2.345.d: तस्य तिस्रो दीक्षास् तिस्र उपसदः समानम् आभिषेकस्य कालात् ।
18.2.345.m: For him there are three consecration days and three upasads. The procedure is identical up to the time of unction.
At the time of unction, he sprinkles him with the residue of the śukra and manthin cups.

18.3.345.s: sthapati sthapatisavena yakṣyamāṇo bhavati sa upakalpayata ārṣabhaṃ carma suvarṇarajatau ca rukmāv audumbaraṃ pātraṃ dadhy abhiṣecanāya
18.3.345.d: स्थपति स्थपतिसवेन यक्ष्यमाणो भवति स उपकल्पयत आर्षभं चर्म सुवर्णरजतौ च रुक्माव् औदुम्बरं पात्रं दध्य् अभिषेचनाय
18.3.345.m: The governor is about to sacrifice with the Sthapatisava. He makes ready a bull's hide, two ornaments of gold and silver, an audumbara vessel, and curds for the unction.

18.3.345.s: dīkṣate tasya tisro dīkṣāstisra upasadas | āgneyasya mārutī pṛśniḥ paṣṭhauhy upālambhyā bhavati
18.3.345.d: दीक्षते तस्य तिस्रो दीक्षास्तिस्र उपसदस् । आग्नेयस्य मारुती पृश्निः पष्ठौह्य् उपालम्भ्या भवति
18.3.345.m: He undergoes consecration. For him there are three consecration days and three upasads. Beside the victim for Agni, a spotted six-year-old cow for the Maruts is to be seized.

18.3.345.s: sapta havīm̐ṣi prātaḥsavanīyān anuvartante yad āgneyo bhavaty agnimukhā hy ṛddhis | ity etāni
18.3.345.d: सप्त हवीँषि प्रातःसवनीयान् अनुवर्तन्ते यद् आग्नेयो भवत्य् अग्निमुखा ह्य् ऋद्धिस् । इत्य् एतानि
18.3.345.m: Seven oblations follow after the morning savanīya oblations: those [beginning with] 'In that it is dedicated to Agni, for success has Agni at its head.'

18.3.345.s: samānam ābhiṣekasya kālāt | abhiṣekasya kāle yajamānāyatana ārṣabhaṃ carma prācīnagrīvam uttaralomopastṛṇāti
18.3.345.d: समानम् आभिषेकस्य कालात् । अभिषेकस्य काले यजमानायतन आर्षभं चर्म प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमोपस्तृणाति
18.3.345.m: The procedure is identical up to the time of unction. At the time of unction, he spreads the bull's hide on the sacrificer's seat, with its neck turned toward the east and its hair upward.

18.3.345.s: tad yajamānaṃ prāñcam upaveśya suvarṇarajatābhyām̐ rukmābhyāṃ paryupāsyaudumbare pātre dadhy ānīyābhiṣiñcati devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyām̐ sarasvatyai vāco yantur yantreṇa sthapatisavenābhiṣiñcāmi | iti
18.3.345.d: तद् यजमानं प्राञ्चम् उपवेश्य सुवर्णरजताभ्याँ रुक्माभ्यां पर्युपास्यौदुम्बरे पात्रे दध्य् आनीयाभिषिञ्चति देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर् बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्याँ सरस्वत्यै वाचो यन्तुर् यन्त्रेण स्थपतिसवेनाभिषिञ्चामि । इति
18.3.345.m: Having seated the sacrificer there facing east, having placed on him the two ornaments of gold and silver, and having brought curds into the audumbara vessel, he sprinkles him, [reciting:] 'On the impulse of the divine Savitar, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, with the restraint of Sarasvatī, the restrainer of speech, with the Sthapatisava I sprinkle you.'

18.3.345.s: samunmṛṣṭe samutkrośantīti samānam ā mukhasya vimārjanāt
18.3.345.d: समुन्मृष्टे समुत्क्रोशन्तीति समानम् आ मुखस्य विमार्जनात्
18.3.345.m: When he is wiped, they shout together; thus it is identical up to the wiping of the face.

18.3.345.s: sa eṣa sthapatisavaḥ saptadaśo 'gniṣṭomas | eṣa hainenātaḥ pūrvam ījire ||
18.3.345.d: स एष स्थपतिसवः सप्तदशो ऽग्निष्टोमस् । एष हैनेनातः पूर्वम् ईजिरे ॥
18.3.345.m: This Sthapatisava is a seventeen-fold agniṣṭoma. With this [sacrifice] indeed they sacrificed previously.

18.4.346.s: sūtaḥ sūtasavena yakṣyamāṇo bhavati sa upakalpayate kṛṣṇājinam̐ suvarṇarajatau ca rukmau parṇamayaṃ pātram̐ hiraṇyaṃ ghṛtam abhiṣecanāya
18.4.346.d: सूतः सूतसवेन यक्ष्यमाणो भवति स उपकल्पयते कृष्णाजिनँ सुवर्णरजतौ च रुक्मौ पर्णमयं पात्रँ हिरण्यं घृतम् अभिषेचनाय
18.4.346.m: The charioteer is about to sacrifice with the Sūtasava. He makes ready a black antelope skin, two ornaments of gold and silver, a vessel of parṇa wood, gold, and clarified butter for the unction.
He undergoes consecration. For him there are three consecration days and three upasads.

18.4.346.s: aṣṭau havīm̐ṣi prātaḥsavanīyān anuvartante yad āgneyo bhavaty āgneyo vai brāhmaṇas | ity etāni
18.4.346.d: अष्टौ हवीँषि प्रातःसवनीयान् अनुवर्तन्ते यद् आग्नेयो भवत्य् आग्नेयो वै ब्राह्मणस् । इत्य् एतानि
18.4.346.m: Eight oblations follow after the morning savanīya oblations: those [beginning with] 'In that it is dedicated to Agni, for the brāhmaṇa is dedicated to Agni.'
[The ritual is] identical up to the time of the consecration.

18.4.346.s: abhiṣekasya kāle yajamānāyatane kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvam uttaralomopastṛṇāti
18.4.346.d: अभिषेकस्य काले यजमानायतने कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमोपस्तृणाति
18.4.346.m: At the time of the consecration, he spreads out a black antelope skin with the neck to the east and the hairy side facing up at the seat of the sacrificer.

18.4.346.s: tad yajamānaṃ prāñcam upaveśya suvarṇarajatābhyām̐ rukmābhyāṃ paryupāsya parṇamaye pātre ghṛtam ānīya hiraṇyenotpūyābhiṣiñcati devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyām̐ sarasvatyai vāco yantur yantreṇa sūtasavenābhiṣiñcāmi | iti
18.4.346.d: तद् यजमानं प्राञ्चम् उपवेश्य सुवर्णरजताभ्याँ रुक्माभ्यां पर्युपास्य पर्णमये पात्रे घृतम् आनीय हिरण्येनोत्पूयाभिषिञ्चति देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर् बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्याँ सरस्वत्यै वाचो यन्तुर् यन्त्रेण सूतसवेनाभिषिञ्चामि । इति
18.4.346.m: Having seated the sacrificer facing east on it, having placed the two gold and silver ornaments on him, having poured clarified butter into a vessel of parṇa wood, and having purified it with gold, he consecrates him with: "At the impulse of the god Savitar, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, by the restraint of Sarasvatī the restrainer of speech, I consecrate you with the Sūtasava."

18.4.346.s: samunmṛṣṭe samutkrośantīti samānam ā mukhasya vimārjanāt
18.4.346.d: समुन्मृष्टे समुत्क्रोशन्तीति समानम् आ मुखस्य विमार्जनात्
18.4.346.m: When he wipes himself, they shout together; [this is] identical up to the wiping of the face.

18.4.346.s: sa eṣa sūtasavaḥ saptadaśo 'gniṣṭomas | eṣa eva sūtasavas |
18.4.346.d: स एष सूतसवः सप्तदशो ऽग्निष्टोमस् । एष एव सूतसवस् ।
18.4.346.m: This is the Sūtasava; it is a seventeen-fold agniṣṭoma. This indeed is the Sūtasava.

18.4.346.s: eṣa grāmaṇīsavas | eṣa ṛtusavas | ṛtavo hainenātaḥ pūrvam ījire ||
18.4.346.d: एष ग्रामणीसवस् । एष ऋतुसवस् । ऋतवो हैनेनातः पूर्वम् ईजिरे ॥
18.4.346.m: This is the Grāmaṇīsava. This is the Ṛtusava. The seasons (ṛtu) indeed sacrificed with this before this.

18.5.346.s: somasavena yakṣyamāṇo bhavati sa upakalpayate saumīm̐ sūtavaśāṃ kṛṣṇājinam̐ suvarṇarajatau ca rukmau parṇamayaṃ pātraṃ payo 'bhiṣecanāya |
18.5.346.d: सोमसवेन यक्ष्यमाणो भवति स उपकल्पयते सौमीँ सूतवशां कृष्णाजिनँ सुवर्णरजतौ च रुक्मौ पर्णमयं पात्रं पयो ऽभिषेचनाय ।
18.5.346.m: When he is about to sacrifice with the Somasava, he procures a barren cow dedicated to Soma, a black antelope skin, two ornaments of gold and silver, a vessel of parṇa wood, and milk for the consecration.

18.5.346.s: atha vai brāhmaṇaṃ bhavati yat kiṃca rājasūyam ṛte somaṃ tat sarvaṃ bhavati | iti
18.5.346.d: अथ वै ब्राह्मणं भवति यत् किंच राजसूयम् ऋते सोमं तत् सर्वं भवति । इति
18.5.346.m: Now indeed there is a brāhmaṇa passage: "Whatever belongs to the Rājasūya, except Soma, all that takes place."

18.5.346.s: sa āmāvāsyena haviṣeṣṭvāṣṭāv ahāny ānumataprabhṛtibhir eti saṃvatsaraṃ cāturmāsyaiḥ saptendraturīyaprabhṛtibhis |
18.5.346.d: स आमावास्येन हविषेष्ट्वाष्टाव् अहान्य् आनुमतप्रभृतिभिर् एति संवत्सरं चातुर्मास्यैः सप्तेन्द्रतुरीयप्रभृतिभिस् ।
18.5.346.m: Having sacrificed with the oblation of the new moon ritual, he proceeds for eight days with [the offerings] beginning with the Ānumata, for a year with the Cāturmāsyas, and with [the offerings] beginning with the Indraturīya.
Then he sacrifices with the oblations of the jewel-bearers (ratnins).
Then he sacrifices with the oblations to the divine quickeners (devasūs).

18.5.347.s: athaitām̐ saumīm̐ sūtavaśām ālabhate tasyā asamudite yajamānāyatane kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvam uttaralomopastṛṇāti
18.5.347.d: अथैताँ सौमीँ सूतवशाम् आलभते तस्या असमुदिते यजमानायतने कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमोपस्तृणाति
18.5.347.m: Then he seizes this barren cow dedicated to Soma. Before its conclusion, he spreads out a black antelope skin with the neck to the east and the hairy side facing up at the seat of the sacrificer.

18.5.347.s: tad yajamānaṃ prāñcam upaveśya suvarṇarajatābhyām̐ rukmābhyāṃ paryupāsya parṇamaye pātre paya ānīyābhiṣiñcati | aṣāḍhaṃ yutsu pṛtanāsu paprim | suvarṣām apsvāṃ vṛjanasya gopām | bhareṣujām̐ sukṣitim̐ suśravasam | jayantaṃ tvāmanu madema soma ||
18.5.347.d: तद् यजमानं प्राञ्चम् उपवेश्य सुवर्णरजताभ्याँ रुक्माभ्यां पर्युपास्य पर्णमये पात्रे पय आनीयाभिषिञ्चति । अषाढं युत्सु पृतनासु पप्रिम् । सुवर्षाम् अप्स्वां वृजनस्य गोपाम् । भरेषुजाँ सुक्षितिँ सुश्रवसम् । जयन्तं त्वामनु मदेम सोम ॥
18.5.347.m: Having seated the sacrificer facing east on it, having placed the two gold and silver ornaments on him, and having poured milk into a vessel of parṇa wood, he consecrates him with: / "Invincible in battles, fulfilling in conflicts, / winning the sun, dwelling in the waters, protector of the host, / born in contests, granting good abode, of great renown, / may we exult after you, victorious Soma!"

18.5.347.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyām̐ sarasvatyai vāco yantur yantreṇa somasavenābhiṣiñcāmi | iti
18.5.347.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर् बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्याँ सरस्वत्यै वाचो यन्तुर् यन्त्रेण सोमसवेनाभिषिञ्चामि । इति
18.5.347.m: "At the impulse of the god Savitar, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, by the restraint of Sarasvatī the restrainer of speech, I consecrate you with the Somasava."

18.5.347.s: samunmṛṣṭe samutkrośantīti samānam ā mukhasya vimārjanāt |
18.5.347.d: समुन्मृष्टे समुत्क्रोशन्तीति समानम् आ मुखस्य विमार्जनात् ।
18.5.347.m: When he wipes himself, they shout together; [this is] identical up to the wiping of the face.

18.5.347.s: atha sam̐sṛpām̐ havirbhir yajate | atha pañcahaviṣā diśām aveṣṭyā yajate |
18.5.347.d: अथ सँसृपाँ हविर्भिर् यजते । अथ पञ्चहविषा दिशाम् अवेष्ट्या यजते ।
18.5.347.m: Then he sacrifices with the Saṃsṛp oblations. Then he sacrifices with the Aveṣṭi of the directions consisting of five oblations.
Then he sacrifices with an animal sacrifice of two animals.

18.5.347.s: atha sātyadūtānām̐ havirbhir yajate | atha pūrvaiḥ prayujām̐ havirbhir yajate |
18.5.347.d: अथ सात्यदूतानाँ हविर्भिर् यजते । अथ पूर्वैः प्रयुजाँ हविर्भिर् यजते ।
18.5.347.m: Then he sacrifices with the oblations of the Sātyadūtas. Then he sacrifices with the former Prayuj oblations.

18.5.347.s: atha paurṇamāsavaimṛdhābhyām iṣṭvottaraiḥ prayujām̐ havirbhir yajate |
18.5.347.d: अथ पौर्णमासवैमृधाभ्याम् इष्ट्वोत्तरैः प्रयुजाँ हविर्भिर् यजते ।
18.5.347.m: Then, having sacrificed with the full moon and Vaimṛdha offerings, he sacrifices with the latter Prayuj oblations.

18.5.347.s: atha devikāhavirbhir yajate | atha traidhātavīyayā yajate |
18.5.347.d: अथ देविकाहविर्भिर् यजते । अथ त्रैधातवीयया यजते ।
18.5.347.m: Then he sacrifices with the Devikā oblations. Then he sacrifices with the Traidhātavīyā offering.

18.5.347.s: atha sautrāmaṇyā yajate saṃtiṣṭhate somasavo 'rdhacaturdaśair māsaiḥ ||
18.5.347.d: अथ सौत्रामण्या यजते संतिष्ठते सोमसवो ऽर्धचतुर्दशैर् मासैः ॥
18.5.347.m: Then he sacrifices with the Sautrāmaṇī. The Somasava is completed in thirteen and a half months.

18.6.347.s: pṛthisavena yakṣyamāṇo bhavati sa upakalpayate rohitaṃ carmānaḍuham̐ suvarṇarajatau ca rukmāv audumbaraṃ droṇaṃ catuḥsrakti catuṣṭayīr apo digbhyaḥ saṃbhṛtās |
18.6.347.d: पृथिसवेन यक्ष्यमाणो भवति स उपकल्पयते रोहितं चर्मानडुहँ सुवर्णरजतौ च रुक्माव् औदुम्बरं द्रोणं चतुःस्रक्ति चतुष्टयीर् अपो दिग्भ्यः संभृतास् ।
18.6.347.m: When he is about to sacrifice with the Pṛthisava, he procures the red hide of an ox, two ornaments of gold and silver, a four-cornered wooden trough of udumbara wood, and the fourfold waters gathered from the directions.
Now indeed there is a brāhmaṇa passage:

18.6.348.s: yat kiṃca rājasūyam anuttaravedīkaṃ tat sarvaṃ bhavati | iti sa āmāvāsyena haviṣeṣṭvāṣṭāv ahāny ānumataprabhṛtibhir eti saptendraturīyaprabhṛtibhis |
18.6.348.d: यत् किंच राजसूयम् अनुत्तरवेदीकं तत् सर्वं भवति । इति स आमावास्येन हविषेष्ट्वाष्टाव् अहान्य् आनुमतप्रभृतिभिर् एति सप्तेन्द्रतुरीयप्रभृतिभिस् ।
18.6.348.m: "Whatever belongs to the Rājasūya that has no high altar, all that takes place." Having sacrificed with the oblation of the new moon ritual, he proceeds for eight days with [the offerings] beginning with the Ānumata, and for seven with those beginning with the Indraturīya.

18.6.348.s: atha ratninām̐ havirbhir yajate | atha devasuvām̐ havirbhir yajate |
18.6.348.d: अथ रत्निनाँ हविर्भिर् यजते । अथ देवसुवाँ हविर्भिर् यजते ।
18.6.348.m: Then he sacrifices with the oblations of the jewel-bearers (ratnins). Then he sacrifices with the oblations to the divine quickeners (devasūs).

18.6.348.s: athaitāṃ caturhaviṣam iṣṭiṃ nirvapaty āgneyam aṣṭākapālam aindram ekādaśakapālaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ bārhaspatyaṃ carum iti
18.6.348.d: अथैतां चतुर्हविषम् इष्टिं निर्वपत्य् आग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालम् ऐन्द्रम् एकादशकपालं वैश्वदेवं द्वादशकपालं बार्हस्पत्यं चरुम् इति
18.6.348.m: Then he distributes this four-oblation offering: an eight-pot-sherd cake for Agni, an eleven-pot-sherd cake for Indra, a twelve-pot-sherd cake for the Viśvedevas, and a mess of boiled rice for Bṛhaspati.

18.6.348.s: tasyā asamudite yajamānāyatane rohitaṃ carmānaḍuhaṃ prācīnagrīvam uttaralomopastṛṇāti
18.6.348.d: तस्या असमुदिते यजमानायतने रोहितं चर्मानडुहं प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमोपस्तृणाति
18.6.348.m: Before its conclusion, he spreads out the red hide of an ox with the neck to the east and the hairy side facing up at the seat of the sacrificer.

18.6.348.s: tad yajamānaṃ prāñcam upaveśya suvarṇarajatābhyām̐ rukmābhyāṃ paryupāsyaudumbare droṇe catuṣṭayīr apaḥ samavanīyābhiṣiñcati ye me pañcāśataṃ dadus | aśvānām̐ sadhastutiḥ | dyumad agne mahi śravas | bṛhat kṛdhi maghonāṃ nṛvad amṛta nṛṇām ||
18.6.348.d: तद् यजमानं प्राञ्चम् उपवेश्य सुवर्णरजताभ्याँ रुक्माभ्यां पर्युपास्यौदुम्बरे द्रोणे चतुष्टयीर् अपः समवनीयाभिषिञ्चति ये मे पञ्चाशतं ददुस् । अश्वानाँ सधस्तुतिः । द्युमद् अग्ने महि श्रवस् । बृहत् कृधि मघोनां नृवद् अमृत नृणाम् ॥
18.6.348.m: Having seated the sacrificer facing east on it, having placed the two gold and silver ornaments on him, and having brought together the fourfold waters into the wooden trough of udumbara wood, he consecrates him with: / "Those who gave fifty horses to me, / in common praise; / splendid, O Agni, great renown, / make high for the bounteous patrons, manly, O immortal, for the men!"

18.6.348.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyām̐ sarasvatyai vāco yantur yantreṇa pṛthisavenābhiṣiñcāmi | iti
18.6.348.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर् बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्याँ सरस्वत्यै वाचो यन्तुर् यन्त्रेण पृथिसवेनाभिषिञ्चामि । इति
18.6.348.m: “At the impulse of god Savitar, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, with the restrainer of speech the restrainer, I consecrate you with the Pṛthisava,” [he says].

18.6.348.s: samunmṛṣṭe samutkrośantīti samānam ā mukhasya vimārjanāt |
18.6.348.d: समुन्मृष्टे समुत्क्रोशन्तीति समानम् आ मुखस्य विमार्जनात् ।
18.6.348.m: When he wipes himself, they shout together; [this is] identical up to the wiping of the face.

18.6.348.s: atha sam̐sṛpām̐ havirbhir yajate | atha pañcahaviṣā diśāmaveṣṭyā yajate |
18.6.348.d: अथ सँसृपाँ हविर्भिर् यजते । अथ पञ्चहविषा दिशामवेष्ट्या यजते ।
18.6.348.m: Then he sacrifices with the Saṃsṛp oblations. Then he sacrifices with the Aveṣṭi of the directions consisting of five oblations.

18.6.348.s: athopātītya dvipaśuṃ paśubandham̐ sātyadūtānām̐ havirbhir yajate |
18.6.348.d: अथोपातीत्य द्विपशुं पशुबन्धँ सात्यदूतानाँ हविर्भिर् यजते ।
18.6.348.m: Then, having passed over the animal sacrifice of two animals, he sacrifices with the oblations of the Sātyadūtas.

18.6.348.s: atha pūrvaiḥ prayujām̐ havirbhir yajate | atha paurṇamāsavaimṛdhābhyām iṣṭvottaraiḥ prayujām̐ havirbhir yajate |
18.6.348.d: अथ पूर्वैः प्रयुजाँ हविर्भिर् यजते । अथ पौर्णमासवैमृधाभ्याम् इष्ट्वोत्तरैः प्रयुजाँ हविर्भिर् यजते ।
18.6.348.m: Then he sacrifices with the former Prayuj oblations. Then, having sacrificed with the full moon and Vaimṛdha offerings, he sacrifices with the latter Prayuj oblations.
Then he sacrifices with the Devikā oblations.

18.6.348.s: atha traidhātavīyayā yajate | atha sautrāmaṇyā yajate
18.6.348.d: अथ त्रैधातवीयया यजते । अथ सौत्रामण्या यजते
18.6.348.m: Then he sacrifices with the Traidhātavīyā offering. Then he sacrifices with the Sautrāmaṇī.
The Pṛthisava is completed in one and a half months.

18.7.349.s: gosavena yakṣyamāṇo bhavati sa upakalpayate 'yutaṃ dakṣiṇāḥ suvarṇarajatau ca rukmau parṇamayaṃ pātraṃ pratidhug abhiṣecanāya
18.7.349.d: गोसवेन यक्ष्यमाणो भवति स उपकल्पयते ऽयुतं दक्षिणाः सुवर्णरजतौ च रुक्मौ पर्णमयं पात्रं प्रतिधुग् अभिषेचनाय
18.7.349.m: When he is about to sacrifice with the Gosava, he procures ten thousand [cows] as sacrificial gifts, two ornaments of gold and silver, a vessel of parṇa wood, and fresh milk for the consecration.

18.7.349.s: dīkṣate tasya ṣaḍ dīkṣāḥ ṣaḍ upasadaḥ samānam ābhiṣekasya kālāt |
18.7.349.d: दीक्षते तस्य षड् दीक्षाः षड् उपसदः समानम् आभिषेकस्य कालात् ।
18.7.349.m: He undergoes consecration. For him there are six dīkṣā days and six upasad days. [The ritual is] identical up to the time of the consecration.

18.7.349.s: abhiṣekasya kāle yajamānāyatane kṛṣṇājinamātraṃ veder anuddhataṃ bhavati
18.7.349.d: अभिषेकस्य काले यजमानायतने कृष्णाजिनमात्रं वेदेर् अनुद्धतं भवति
18.7.349.m: At the time of the consecration, a spot the size of a black antelope skin is left unexcavated from the altar at the seat of the sacrificer.

18.7.349.s: tad yajamānaṃ prāñcam upaveśya suvarṇarajatābhyām̐ rukmābhyāṃ paryupāsya parṇamaye pātre pratidhug ānīya bṛhata stotraṃ pratyabhiṣiñcati revaj jātaḥ sahasā vṛddhaḥ kṣatrāṇāṃ kṣatrabhṛttamo vayodhāḥ | mahān mahitve tastabhānaḥ kṣatre rāṣṭre ca jāgṛhi | prajāpates tvā parameṣṭhinaḥ svārājyenābhiṣiñcāmi ||
18.7.349.d: तद् यजमानं प्राञ्चम् उपवेश्य सुवर्णरजताभ्याँ रुक्माभ्यां पर्युपास्य पर्णमये पात्रे प्रतिधुग् आनीय बृहत स्तोत्रं प्रत्यभिषिञ्चति रेवज् जातः सहसा वृद्धः क्षत्राणां क्षत्रभृत्तमो वयोधाः । महान् महित्वे तस्तभानः क्षत्रे राष्ट्रे च जागृहि । प्रजापतेस् त्वा परमेष्ठिनः स्वाराज्येनाभिषिञ्चामि ॥
18.7.349.m: Having seated the sacrificer facing east on it, having placed the two gold and silver ornaments on him, and having poured fresh milk into a vessel of parṇa wood, he consecrates him towards the Bṛhat-stotra: / "Born rich, grown through strength, / best bearer of dominion among dominions, bestower of vigour, / great, firm in your greatness, / be watchful over dominion and realm! / I consecrate you with the sovereignty of Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin!"

18.7.349.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyām̐ sarasvatyai vāco yantur yantreṇa gosavenābhiṣiñcāmi | iti
18.7.349.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर् बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्याँ सरस्वत्यै वाचो यन्तुर् यन्त्रेण गोसवेनाभिषिञ्चामि । इति
18.7.349.m: "At the impulse of the god Savitar, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, by the restraint of Sarasvatī the restrainer of speech, I consecrate you with the Gosava."

18.7.349.s: samunmṛṣṭe samutkrośantīti samānam ā mukhasya vimārjanāt
18.7.349.d: समुन्मृष्टे समुत्क्रोशन्तीति समानम् आ मुखस्य विमार्जनात्
18.7.349.m: When he wipes himself, they shout together; [this is] identical up to the wiping of the face.

18.7.349.s: sa eṣa gosavaḥ ṣaṭtrim̐śaḥ sarva ukthya ubhayasāmāyutadakṣiṇaḥ
18.7.349.d: स एष गोसवः षट्त्रिँशः सर्व उक्थ्य उभयसामायुतदक्षिणः
18.7.349.m: This Gosava is thirty-six-fold, completely an ukthya, having both sāmans, with a sacrificial gift of ten thousand [cows].
At the Pavamāna chant they execute the Kaṇvarathaṃtara saman.

18.8.349.s: odanasavena yakṣyamāṇo bhavati sa upakalpayate rohitaṃ carmānaḍuham̐ suvarṇarajatau ca rukmau śatamānaṃ ca pravartaṃ caturo varṇān brāhmaṇam̐ rājanyaṃ vaiśyam̐ śūdraṃ caturo rasān madhu surāṃ paya apaś catvāri pātrāṇi sauvarṇam̐ rājataṃ kām̐syaṃ mṛnmayaṃ catasro dakṣiṇāḥ śatamānam̐ hiraṇyaṃ tisṛdhanvamaṣṭrāṃ māṣaiḥ pūrṇaṃ kamaṇḍaluṃ catuṣṭayīḥ śalākāḥ parṇamayyau naiyagrodhyāv āśvatthyau phālgunapācyau catvāri nānāvṛkṣyāṇi pātrāṇi saktūm̐s trīṇi darbhapuñjīlāny audumbaraṃ droṇaṃ catuḥsrakti catuṣaṭayīr apo digbhyaḥ saṃbhṛtāḥ śataṃ ca rathaṃ ca |
18.8.349.d: ओदनसवेन यक्ष्यमाणो भवति स उपकल्पयते रोहितं चर्मानडुहँ सुवर्णरजतौ च रुक्मौ शतमानं च प्रवर्तं चतुरो वर्णान् ब्राह्मणँ राजन्यं वैश्यँ शूद्रं चतुरो रसान् मधु सुरां पय अपश् चत्वारि पात्राणि सौवर्णँ राजतं काँस्यं मृन्मयं चतस्रो दक्षिणाः शतमानँ हिरण्यं तिसृधन्वमष्ट्रां माषैः पूर्णं कमण्डलुं चतुष्टयीः शलाकाः पर्णमय्यौ नैयग्रोध्याव् आश्वत्थ्यौ फाल्गुनपाच्यौ चत्वारि नानावृक्ष्याणि पात्राणि सक्तूँस् त्रीणि दर्भपुञ्जीलान्य् औदुम्बरं द्रोणं चतुःस्रक्ति चतुषटयीर् अपो दिग्भ्यः संभृताः शतं च रथं च ।
18.8.349.m: When he is going to sacrifice with the odanasava, he procures: a red ox-hide, two gold and silver plates, a round ear-ornament of a hundred measures, the four classes—a brāhmaṇa, a rājanya, a vaiśya, and a śūdra—four fluids—honey, surā, milk, and water—four vessels—golden, silver, bronze, and earthenware—four sacrificial gifts: gold of a hundred measures, a bow with three arrows, a goad, a water-pot filled with beans; four kinds of stirring-sticks: two of parṇa-wood, two of nyagrodha-wood, two of aśvattha-wood, and two of phālgunapācī-wood; four vessels of different kinds of wood, barley-groats, three bunches of darbha grass, a four-cornered wooden tub of udumbara-wood, four kinds of waters collected from the quarters, a hundred [cows], and a chariot.

18.8.350.m: With this having been procured, he rests until the Rohiṇī [constellation] approaches.

18.8.350.s: atha rohiṇyeti pūrvāgnim anvavasyaty uttapanīyam̐ śālīno 'nvāhāryapacanam āhitāgnis |
18.8.350.d: अथ रोहिण्येति पूर्वाग्निम् अन्ववस्यत्य् उत्तपनीयँ शालीनो ऽन्वाहार्यपचनम् आहिताग्निस् ।
18.8.350.m: Then, under Rohiṇī, one who has a house establishes the heating-fire from the eastern fire, while one who has consecrated his fires [establishes] the anvāhāryapacana fire.

18.8.350.s: athādhvaryur apararātra ādrutya sam̐śāsti | ekaudanam̐ śrapayata | iti
18.8.350.d: अथाध्वर्युर् अपररात्र आद्रुत्य सँशास्ति । एकौदनँ श्रपयत । इति
18.8.350.m: Then, having hastened in the latter part of the night, the adhvaryu priest instructs: 'Cook the single pot of boiled rice!'

18.8.350.s: taṃ tathā śrapayanti yathā purādityasyodayāc chṛto bhavati |
18.8.350.d: तं तथा श्रपयन्ति यथा पुरादित्यस्योदयाच् छृतो भवति ।
18.8.350.m: They cook it in such a way that it is cooked before the rising of the sun.

18.8.350.s: udyatā sūryeṇa kāryas | iti brāhmaṇam athaitam odanam̐ śrapayitvābhighāryodañcam udvāsayati |
18.8.350.d: उद्यता सूर्येण कार्यस् । इति ब्राह्मणम् अथैतम् ओदनँ श्रपयित्वाभिघार्योदञ्चम् उद्वासयति ।
18.8.350.m: 'It is to be performed while the sun is rising,' says the brāhmaṇa passage. Then, having cooked this boiled rice and having basted it with clarified butter, he takes it down towards the north.

18.8.350.s: athaitāṃ pātrīṃ nirṇijyopastīrya tasyām enam asaṃghnann ivoddharati
18.8.350.d: अथैतां पात्रीं निर्णिज्योपस्तीर्य तस्याम् एनम् असंघ्नन्न् इवोद्धरति
18.8.350.m: Then, having washed this dish and having strewn [it with grass], he takes it out into it without breaking it apart, as it were,

18.8.350.s: sarpir āsecanaṃ kṛtvā prabhūtam ājyam ānīya |
18.8.350.d: सर्पिर् आसेचनं कृत्वा प्रभूतम् आज्यम् आनीय ।
18.8.350.m: having made a cavity for pouring melted butter and having poured in abundant clarified butter.

18.8.350.s: athaitām̐ś caturo varṇān dakṣiṇata udaṅmukhān upaveśayati |
18.8.350.d: अथैताँश् चतुरो वर्णान् दक्षिणत उदङ्मुखान् उपवेशयति ।
18.8.350.m: Then he seats these four classes to the south, facing north.

18.8.350.s: athānvārabdhe yajamāne juhoti sim̐he vyāghra uta yā pṛdākau | iti catasraḥ sruvāhutīs |
18.8.350.d: अथान्वारब्धे यजमाने जुहोति सिँहे व्याघ्र उत या पृदाकौ । इति चतस्रः स्रुवाहुतीस् ।
18.8.350.m: Then, while the sacrificer holds on from behind, he offers four ladle libations with [the verse beginning]: 'That which is in the lion, the tiger, and in the adder...'

18.8.351.s: hutvāhutvaiva sam̐srāvaiḥ pravartam abhighārayati rāḍ asi virāḍ asi samrāḍ asi svarāḍ asi | iti |
18.8.351.d: हुत्वाहुत्वैव सँस्रावैः प्रवर्तम् अभिघारयति राड् असि विराड् असि सम्राड् असि स्वराड् असि । इति ।
18.8.351.m: Immediately after each offering, he sprinkles the round ear-ornament with the residues [saying]: 'A ruler art thou, a wide ruler art thou, a sovereign ruler art thou, a self-ruler art thou!'

18.8.351.s: athaitaṃ pravartam agreṇāhavanīyaṃ paryāhṛtya dakṣiṇato nidadhāti ||
18.8.351.d: अथैतं प्रवर्तम् अग्रेणाहवनीयं पर्याहृत्य दक्षिणतो निदधाति ॥
18.8.351.m: Then, having brought this round ear-ornament around in front of the āhavanīya fire, he places it down to the south.

18.9.351.s: athaitat sauvarṇaṃ pātraṃ yācati tasmim̐s tiraḥ pavitraṃ madhv ānīya saktūn opya parṇamayībhyām̐ śalākābhyām upamanthati | indrāya tvā tejasvate tejasvantam̐ śrīṇāmi | iti
18.9.351.d: अथैतत् सौवर्णं पात्रं याचति तस्मिँस् तिरः पवित्रं मध्व् आनीय सक्तून् ओप्य पर्णमयीभ्याँ शलाकाभ्याम् उपमन्थति । इन्द्राय त्वा तेजस्वते तेजस्वन्तँ श्रीणामि । इति
18.9.351.m: Then he asks for this golden vessel. Having poured honey into it across the purifier and having strewn barley-groats, he stirs it with the two stirring-sticks of parṇa-wood, saying: 'For fiery Indra, I mix thee endowed with fiery energy!'
'Thou art fiery energy!' [saying thus], he hands it over to the brāhmaṇa.

18.9.351.s: tat te prayacchāmi | iti brāhmaṇaḥ pratigṛhṇāti | atha yajamāno mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe tejasvad astu me mukham | tejasvac chiro astu me | tejasvān viśvataḥ pratyaṅ tejasā saṃpipṛgdhi mā | iti
18.9.351.d: तत् ते प्रयच्छामि । इति ब्राह्मणः प्रतिगृह्णाति । अथ यजमानो मुखं विमृष्टे तेजस्वद् अस्तु मे मुखम् । तेजस्वच् छिरो अस्तु मे । तेजस्वान् विश्वतः प्रत्यङ् तेजसा संपिपृग्धि मा । इति
18.9.351.m: 'That I hand over to thee,' saying thus the brāhmaṇa receives it. Then the sacrificer wipes his face [saying]: 'Endowed with fiery energy be my face! / Endowed with fiery energy be my head! / Endowed with fiery energy from all sides facing within, / unite me with fiery energy!'

18.9.351.s: trir ācamya praśam̐sati tasmā etac caiva pātraṃ dadāti śatamānaṃ ca hiraṇyam
18.9.351.d: त्रिर् आचम्य प्रशँसति तस्मा एतच् चैव पात्रं ददाति शतमानं च हिरण्यम्
18.9.351.m: Having sipped water three times, he pronounces praise. He gives him this very vessel and gold of a hundred measures.

18.9.351.s: athaitad rājataṃ pātraṃ yācati tasmim̐s tiraḥ pavitram̐ surām ānīya saktūn opya naiyagrodhībhyām̐ śalākābhyām upamanthati | indrāya tvaujasvata ojasvantam̐ śrīṇāmi | iti |
18.9.351.d: अथैतद् राजतं पात्रं याचति तस्मिँस् तिरः पवित्रँ सुराम् आनीय सक्तून् ओप्य नैयग्रोधीभ्याँ शलाकाभ्याम् उपमन्थति । इन्द्राय त्वौजस्वत ओजस्वन्तँ श्रीणामि । इति ।
18.9.351.m: Then he asks for this silver vessel. Having poured surā into it across the purifier and having strewn barley-groats, he stirs it with the two stirring-sticks of nyagrodha-wood, saying: 'For mighty Indra, I mix thee endowed with might!'
'Thou art might!' [saying thus], he hands it over to the rājanya.

18.9.351.s: tat te prayacchāmi | iti rājanyaḥ pratigṛhṇāti | atha yajamāno mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe | ojasvad astu me mukham ojasvac chiro astu me | ojasvān viśvataḥ pratyaṅ | ojasā saṃpipṛgdhi mā | iti
18.9.351.d: तत् ते प्रयच्छामि । इति राजन्यः प्रतिगृह्णाति । अथ यजमानो मुखं विमृष्टे । ओजस्वद् अस्तु मे मुखम् ओजस्वच् छिरो अस्तु मे । ओजस्वान् विश्वतः प्रत्यङ् । ओजसा संपिपृग्धि मा । इति
18.9.351.m: 'That I hand over to thee,' saying thus the rājanya receives it. Then the sacrificer wipes his face [saying]: 'Endowed with might be my face! / Endowed with might be my head! / Endowed with might from all sides facing within, / unite me with might!'

18.9.351.s: trir ācamya praśam̐sati tamā etac caiva pātraṃ dadāti tisṛdhanvaṃ ca |
18.9.351.d: त्रिर् आचम्य प्रशँसति तमा एतच् चैव पात्रं ददाति तिसृधन्वं च ।
18.9.351.m: Having sipped water three times, he pronounces praise. He gives him this very vessel and a bow with three arrows.

18.9.351.s: athaitat kām̐syaṃ pātraṃ yācati tasmim̐s tiraḥ pavitraṃ paya ānīya saktūn opyāśvatthībhyām̐ śalākābhyām upamanthati | indrāya tvā payasvate payasvantam̐ śrīṇāmi | iti
18.9.351.d: अथैतत् काँस्यं पात्रं याचति तस्मिँस् तिरः पवित्रं पय आनीय सक्तून् ओप्याश्वत्थीभ्याँ शलाकाभ्याम् उपमन्थति । इन्द्राय त्वा पयस्वते पयस्वन्तँ श्रीणामि । इति
18.9.351.m: Then he asks for this bronze vessel. Having poured milk into it across the purifier and having strewn barley-groats, he stirs it with the two stirring-sticks of aśvattha-wood, saying: 'For Indra endowed with nourishment, I mix thee endowed with nourishment!'
'Thou art nourishment!' [saying thus], he hands it over to the vaiśya.

18.9.352.s: tat te prayacchāmi | iti vaiśyaḥ pratigṛhṇāti | atha yajamāno mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe payasvad astu me mukham | payasvac chiro astu me | payasvān viśvataḥ pratyaṅ payasā saṃpipṛgdhi mā | iti
18.9.352.d: तत् ते प्रयच्छामि । इति वैश्यः प्रतिगृह्णाति । अथ यजमानो मुखं विमृष्टे पयस्वद् अस्तु मे मुखम् । पयस्वच् छिरो अस्तु मे । पयस्वान् विश्वतः प्रत्यङ् पयसा संपिपृग्धि मा । इति
18.9.352.m: 'That I hand over to thee,' saying thus the vaiśya receives it. Then the sacrificer wipes his face [saying]: 'Endowed with nourishment be my face! / Endowed with nourishment be my head! / Endowed with nourishment from all sides facing within, / unite me with nourishment!'
Having sipped water three times, he pronounces praise.

18.9.352.s: tasmā etac caiva pātraṃ dadāty aṣṭrāṃ ca | athaitan mṛnmayaṃ pātraṃ yācati
18.9.352.d: तस्मा एतच् चैव पात्रं ददात्य् अष्ट्रां च । अथैतन् मृन्मयं पात्रं याचति
18.9.352.m: He gives him this very vessel and a goad. Then he asks for this earthenware vessel.

18.9.352.s: tasmim̐s tiraḥ pavitram apa ānīya saktūn opya phālgunapācībhyām̐ śalākābhyām upamanthati | indrāya tvāyuṣmata āyuṣmantam̐ śrīṇāmi | iti |
18.9.352.d: तस्मिँस् तिरः पवित्रम् अप आनीय सक्तून् ओप्य फाल्गुनपाचीभ्याँ शलाकाभ्याम् उपमन्थति । इन्द्राय त्वायुष्मत आयुष्मन्तँ श्रीणामि । इति ।
18.9.352.m: Having poured water into it across the purifier and having strewn barley-groats, he stirs it with the two stirring-sticks of phālgunapācī-wood, saying: 'For long-lived Indra, I mix thee endowed with lifespan!'

18.9.352.s: āyur asi | iti śūdrāya prayacchati tat te prayacchāmi | iti śūdraḥ pratigṛhṇāti |
18.9.352.d: आयुर् असि । इति शूद्राय प्रयच्छति तत् ते प्रयच्छामि । इति शूद्रः प्रतिगृह्णाति ।
18.9.352.m: 'Thou art lifespan!' [saying thus], he hands it over to the śūdra. 'That I hand over to thee,' saying thus the śūdra receives it.

18.9.352.s: atha yajamāno mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe | āyuṣmad astu me mukham āyuṣmac chiro astu me | āyuṣmān viśvataḥ pratyaṅ | āyuṣā saṃpipṛgdhi mā | iti
18.9.352.d: अथ यजमानो मुखं विमृष्टे । आयुष्मद् अस्तु मे मुखम् आयुष्मच् छिरो अस्तु मे । आयुष्मान् विश्वतः प्रत्यङ् । आयुषा संपिपृग्धि मा । इति
18.9.352.m: Then the sacrificer wipes his face [saying]: 'Endowed with lifespan be my face! / Endowed with lifespan be my head! / Endowed with lifespan from all sides facing within, / unite me with lifespan!'

18.9.352.s: trir ācamya praśam̐sati tasmā etac caiva pātraṃ dadāti māṣaiś ca pūrṇaṃ kamaṇḍalum
18.9.352.d: त्रिर् आचम्य प्रशँसति तस्मा एतच् चैव पात्रं ददाति माषैश् च पूर्णं कमण्डलुम्
18.9.352.m: Having sipped water three times, he pronounces praise. He gives him this very vessel and the water-pot filled with beans.
Then, having crept forward to this boiled rice, he eats it.

18.9.352.s: tasya yan na sahate tad apsu praveśayati | atha hiraṇyād ghṛtaṃ niṣpibati
18.9.352.d: तस्य यन् न सहते तद् अप्सु प्रवेशयति । अथ हिरण्याद् घृतं निष्पिबति
18.9.352.m: What of it he cannot finish, he causes that to enter the water. Then he drinks the clarified butter from the gold [plate].

18.9.352.s: niṣpibantam anumantrayate | imam agna āyuṣe varcase kṛdhi priyam̐ reto varuṇa soma rājan | mātevāsmā adite śarma yaccha viśve devā jaradaṣṭir yathāsat | iti |
18.9.352.d: निष्पिबन्तम् अनुमन्त्रयते । इमम् अग्न आयुषे वर्चसे कृधि प्रियँ रेतो वरुण सोम राजन् । मातेवास्मा अदिते शर्म यच्छ विश्वे देवा जरदष्टिर् यथासत् । इति ।
18.9.352.m: As he is drinking it down, he recites over him: 'Make this man, O Agni, for lifespan and splendour, / a dear seed, O Varuṇa, O King Soma! / Grant him refuge like a mother, O Aditi, / and all ye gods, that he may reach old age!'

18.9.352.s: athaitaṃ pravartam adbhiḥ prakṣālya dakṣiṇe karṇa ābadhnīte | āyuṣ ṭe viśvato dadhat | iti |
18.9.352.d: अथैतं प्रवर्तम् अद्भिः प्रक्षाल्य दक्षिणे कर्ण आबध्नीते । आयुष् टे विश्वतो दधत् । इति ।
18.9.352.m: Then, having washed this round ear-ornament with water, he fastens it on his right ear, saying: 'Placing life in thee from every side...'

18.9.352.s: athainam anuparivartayate | āyur asi viśvāyur asi sarvāyur asi sarvam āyur asi | iti |
18.9.352.d: अथैनम् अनुपरिवर्तयते । आयुर् असि विश्वायुर् असि सर्वायुर् असि सर्वम् आयुर् असि । इति ।
18.9.352.m: Then he turns it around, saying: 'Lifespan art thou; universal lifespan art thou; all-lifespan art thou; the whole lifespan art thou!'

18.9.352.s: athainaṃ tribhir darbhapuñjīlaiḥ pavayati yato vāto manojavās | yataḥ kṣaranti sindhavaḥ | tāsāṃ tvā sarvāsām̐ rucā | abhiṣiñcāmi varcasā | iti |
18.9.352.d: अथैनं त्रिभिर् दर्भपुञ्जीलैः पवयति यतो वातो मनोजवास् । यतः क्षरन्ति सिन्धवः । तासां त्वा सर्वासाँ रुचा । अभिषिञ्चामि वर्चसा । इति ।
18.9.352.m: Then he purifies him with three bunches of darbha grass, saying: 'From where the wind swift as thought, / from where the streams flow, / with the lustre of all of them / do I sprinkle thee with splendour!'

18.9.353.s: athāsya dakṣiṇam akṣikaṭaṃ nyacati samudra ivāsi gahmanā soma ivāsy adābhyaḥ | agnir iva viśvataḥ pratyaṅ sūrya iva jyotiṣā vibhūs | iti ||
18.9.353.d: अथास्य दक्षिणम् अक्षिकटं न्यचति समुद्र इवासि गह्मना सोम इवास्य् अदाभ्यः । अग्निर् इव विश्वतः प्रत्यङ् सूर्य इव ज्योतिषा विभूस् । इति ॥
18.9.353.m: Then he touches the outer corner of his right eye, saying: 'Like an ocean art thou in depth; / like Soma art thou, unassailable; / like Agni, facing inwards from all sides; / like the sun, shining brightly with light!'

18.10.353.s: yāvad evātrādhvaryuś ceṣṭati tāvad eṣa pratiprasthātaudumbare droṇe catuṣṭayīr apaḥ samavanīya caturo grahān gṛhṇāti | apāṃ yo dravaṇe rasas tam aham asmā āmuṣyāyaṇāya tejase brahmavarcasāya gṛhṇāmi | iti parṇamayena |
18.10.353.d: यावद् एवात्राध्वर्युश् चेष्टति तावद् एष प्रतिप्रस्थातौदुम्बरे द्रोणे चतुष्टयीर् अपः समवनीय चतुरो ग्रहान् गृह्णाति । अपां यो द्रवणे रसस् तम् अहम् अस्मा आमुष्यायणाय तेजसे ब्रह्मवर्चसाय गृह्णामि । इति पर्णमयेन ।
18.10.353.m: Just as the adhvaryu priest is engaged here, so the pratiprasthātṛ priest, having poured the four kinds of water together into the tub of udumbara-wood, draws four cups, [saying]: 'The sap of the waters that is in their running, that I draw for this descendant of so-and-so for fiery energy and brāhmanic lustre,' with the [vessel] made of parṇa-wood;

18.10.353.s: apāṃ ya ūrmau rasas tam aham asmā āmuṣyāyaṇāyaujase vīryāya gṛhṇāmi | iti naiyagrodhena |
18.10.353.d: अपां य ऊर्मौ रसस् तम् अहम् अस्मा आमुष्यायणायौजसे वीर्याय गृह्णामि । इति नैयग्रोधेन ।
18.10.353.m: 'The sap of the waters that is in the wave, that I draw for this descendant of so-and-so for might and valour,' with the [vessel] made of nyagrodha-wood;

18.10.353.s: apāṃ yo madhyato rasas tam aham asmā āmuṣyāyaṇāya puṣṭyai prajananāya gṛhṇāmi | ity āśvatthena |
